skills.markdown:
---
name: delivery-status
description: 'Continuous delivery documentation for Estate engagements: the weekly client status report, stewardship of the RAID and decision logs with stable IDs, and scope-drift detection against the SOW baseline that raises change-order candidates with an evidence trail. Use for a weekly or project status report, delivery update, what moved this week, logging a decision or risk from a meeting, updating the RAID log, or checking did we agree to that in scope. Do NOT use for authoring change orders or SOWs (statement-of-work), kickoff or charter (delivery-kickoff), UAT tracking (acceptance-testing), pricing (the Estate Pricing System), or sales pursuits (call-prep).'
---


# Estate delivery status

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../writing-integrity/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Keep the engagement record honest, week after week. Three jobs, always together: issue the status report from the record, steward the RAID and decision logs so nothing is re-litigated, and compare observed work against the SOW scope baseline so drift is flagged with evidence before it eats margin. Undocumented decisions cause the same conversation twice; unflagged drift becomes a change order handled reactively or, worse, absorbed silently.

Use the invocation actually configured for the engagement. A reporting cadence does not establish an automatic trigger; require configuration and run evidence before reporting that a scheduled or event-driven update occurred. Every run states exactly what period it covers and reconciles against the previous status file on disk, not against memory of a prior session.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Inputs at a glance

| Input | Role | If missing |
|-------|------|------------|
| Meeting transcripts for the period | Evidence for log entries, drift, and quotes | Named gap in the report; ask the user what happened |
| RAID log and decision log | The record this skill stewards | Stop; offer to seed per `references/log-stewardship.md` |
| SOW scope baseline (scope body + Exhibit A) | The drift comparison target | Drift degrades to "no baseline on file", flagged |
| Previous status file | Reconciliation baseline | State this is the first status |
| Timesheet export or quote (Q-number) | The only legitimate burn source | Burn becomes a named gap, never an estimate |
| The user | Owner assignments, off-transcript events, decisions | Entries stay proposed, not written |

## Governance this skill delegates

- **evidence-core** owns provenance. Every log entry and every status claim carries a named source with a date. An absent fact is a named gap with an owner and a resolve-by date, never a blank or a plausible fill.
- **writing-integrity** owns writing review; a confirmed profile supplies voice. Run its checker on the finished status report. No em dashes, sentence-case headings, counts not adjectives.
- **brand-renderer** owns brand if the status ships as anything beyond markdown. The markdown report itself needs no brand pass.
- **The money rule.** Burn, remaining hours, and fee figures come from a timesheet export, the quote (Q-number), or an explicit user-supplied source. If no source is available this period, the figure is a named gap ("burn unavailable: no timesheet export provided, owner: Program Lead"). Never estimate burn silently. Never compute remaining from memory of last week's number.

Portability fallback: if a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did. Never silently skip.

## Phase 0: orient and pin the period

Pin all five before writing anything:

1. **The engagement.** Client, engagement name, SOW identifier. From the kickoff record or the user.
2. **The period.** Explicit start and end dates. Ask if ambiguous. The report header carries `Period: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD`; the gate fails without it.
3. **The previous status file.** Find it in the engagement folder and read it. Open items, RAID counts, and last-reported burn come from that file. If none exists, say this is the first status of the engagement and that there is no prior baseline to reconcile against.
4. **The governance logs.** The RAID log and decision log seeded at kickoff by `delivery-kickoff`, using the stable ID convention in `references/log-stewardship.md` (R-001, A-001, I-001, D-001 for RAID, where D is a dependency; DEC-001 for decisions). If the logs do not exist, stop and offer to seed them per that reference before producing any status.
5. **The SOW scope baseline.** The signed SOW's scope section and its Exhibit A Basis of Estimate where one exists. Without a baseline, scope-drift detection degrades to "no baseline on file" as a named gap, flagged in the report, not skipped.

## Phase 1: harvest the period's evidence

Read the meeting transcripts for the period verbatim, never summaries. A summary says "the client raised integration concerns"; the transcript says who asked for a second ERP integration and in which sentence. Pull direct quotes and attribute them by speaker and date; quotes are what make a drift flag or a decision entry defensible when it is challenged.

Also gather: the timesheet or burn source for the period, any artifact or gate movement (documents delivered, sign-offs obtained), and anything the user says happened off-transcript (record it as user-reported, with the user as the source).

Where transcripts live in Granola, Drive, or Slack, read what is actually there through the available integrations. Never substitute a similarly titled meeting for the one that was named.

## Phase 2: steward the logs

Rules in full in `references/log-stewardship.md`. The short version:

- **Append-only.** New entries get the next sequential ID. Existing entries are never renumbered, deleted, or rewritten; a correction is a new dated status line on the entry.
- **Every entry sourced.** Transcript quote with speaker and date, SOW clause, or a named person's statement. An unsourced item is proposed to the user, not written.
- **Every entry owned and dated.** Owner, status, resolve-by date, and the gate it blocks where applicable. Unowned actions evaporate.
- **Closure needs a sourced basis.** Never close a risk or mark a decision superseded because it stopped being mentioned. No source, stays open.
- Extract from each transcript: decisions made, new risks, new issues, new dependencies, assumptions stated as fact, and action items. Propose the batch to the user before appending when running interactively.

## Phase 3: detect scope drift

Protocol and evidence-trail format in `references/scope-drift-protocol.md`. The posture:

Compare every observed work item and client ask from the period against the SOW scope baseline. Classify using the Basis of Estimate trigger taxonomy in the contract scope and obligation review mode of `statement-of-work` (read `_runtime/sow-quality/references/basis-of-estimate.md` from that package; the selected agreement controls its applicability): **soft triggers** are volumetric, footprint materially exceeding Exhibit A; **hard triggers** are binary workstream additions such as a second integration or org, which trigger regardless of size.

When drift is found, raise a **change-order CANDIDATE**: the ask quoted verbatim with attribution, the baseline clause it exceeds cited by section, the trigger class, and the routing (Program Lead and CSE). That is the whole move. This skill never decides in-scope versus out-of-scope (a human call), never silently absorbs the work into status as if it were baseline, and never authors the change order itself; contractual review uses the contract scope and obligation review mode in `statement-of-work`, while authorized humans own contractual changes.

A period with no drift still gets a scope-drift section reading "None observed" with a one-line statement of what was compared. The gate requires the section either way; silence is not evidence of a check.

## Phase 4: write the status report

Fill `assets/weekly-status-template.md`. Section spec, ordering rules, and worked line examples in `references/status-report-spec.md`. The rules that carry it:

- **Outcome-first.** Lead with what the client can now do or decide, not with activity. "UAT entry criteria met" beats "the team worked on testing".
- **Counts, not adjectives.** "3 risks open, 1 new, 1 closed" rather than "good progress on risks". Every RAID and decision reference in the report uses its stable ID so the reader can find it in the log.
- **Red flags never buried.** Anything red or newly slipped goes in the flags section at the top of the report, stated plainly with its ID. A banner over a stale document body is not resolution: if a flag is cleared, the body lines that referenced it change too.
- **Every line about scope, hours, or dates carries a source.** Transcript, SOW clause, timesheet export, log entry ID, or a named gap.
- **Reconcile against the previous status.** Items reported open last period are either moved with a sourced basis or restated as still open. An item that vanishes between reports without explanation is the failure mode.

## Phase 5: gate before issuing

```bash
python3 scripts/status_check.py STATUS.md --raid-log RAID.md --decision-log DECISIONS.md
```

The gate is blocking. It verifies: the period is stated in the header; every stable ID referenced in the report exists in the corresponding log file; the scope-drift section is present and is either "None observed" or candidates each carrying at least one evidence citation; the hours-and-burn section names a source or a named gap; and no unfilled placeholders remain. Exit 0 passes; nonzero blocks issue. Report the counts it prints, not an adjective, and write a one-line disposition.

Review the report with `writing-integrity` and run its bundled internal `prose-pass` diagnostics. If the diagnostics are unavailable, state the manual checks actually performed.

## Worked example, end to end

Input: a requirements-session transcript in which the client asks for a NetSuite integration; the SOW names a single integration (Workday). Correct output across the three jobs:

1. **Logs**: a dependency entry (D-0NN, client to confirm whether NetSuite is a requirement or a wish, owner and resolve-by date) and, if a human decided anything in the room, a decision entry. No decision entry for the ask itself; nobody decided anything yet.
2. **Drift**: a candidate block in the scope-drift section. Trigger class hard, the ask quoted verbatim with speaker and date, the SOW integration clause cited by section and quoted, at least one evidence line, routed to Program Lead and CSE.
3. **Status**: the candidate appears in the flags section as well as the scope-drift section, because it needs a decision. It reappears every period until a decision lands and gets a D-0NN.

The wrong outputs, for contrast: logging it as an action item for the team (silent absorption), deciding it is out of scope in the report (a human call), or drafting the change order (authorized humans own contractual changes; the contract scope and obligation review mode in `statement-of-work` reviews the resulting terms).

## State discipline

- Record IDs and quote totals are not durable anchors across sandbox refreshes. Stamp the report with its source objects and as-of dates: the SOW identifier and signed date, the timesheet export date, the transcript dates, the previous status filename.
- Truth hierarchy when sources disagree: signed SOW and its exhibits > governance logs > previous status file > chat context > memory. A conflict between them is flagged in the report, never silently resolved; show both and say which the report uses and why.
- Never hand-patch an issued report. Fix the log or the source, regenerate, and reissue with a new issue date; otherwise the next cadence run resurrects the error.

## Running unattended

Phases 2 and 3 normally propose before appending. On a scheduled or headless run: append log entries with a clearly marked `proposed` status, produce the report, run the gate, and state in the flags section that the proposed entries and any drift candidates await human review. Never record a decision nobody made, never close a RAID item unattended, and never issue the report to the client without a human in the loop; leave it as a draft for the Program Lead.

## Phase 6: land it

If any lifecycle gate moved this period, verify the engagement's DELIVERY-STATE.md reflects it (status, date, append-only log line) per delivery-suite's `references/delivery-state-spec.md`; a stale state file is a flag in the report.

Deliver the report, and commit the report plus the updated logs to the engagement folder so the next cadence run can find them; the previous-status reconciliation in Phase 0 depends on this. Name the report with the period end date (`status-2026-08-08.md`) so ordering is unambiguous. Close with the user on: the flags, any change-order candidates raised, and the biggest judgment call of the period argued from both sides.

Status reports are issued, not signed. Drift flags are proposals for a human decision.

## Durable output

The status report is the run's durable Markdown record and follows `_shared/output-contract.md`: the period, the sources used, the counts, the flags, and the change-order candidates all live in the file, named by period end date and committed to the engagement folder. A run that stops before issuing still leaves a record of what was checked and what blocked it. Deliver or link the file; never just say it was written.

## When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: (1) the narrative accomplishments detail, keep the outcome bullets; (2) upcoming-period detail beyond the next gate; (3) artifact-register updates beyond what moved. Never cut: the period header, log stewardship for decisions and new risks, the scope-drift section, sourcing, or the gate.

## Boundaries

In the delivery chain (SOW, then s2d-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then UAT, then cutover-closeout), this skill's upstream producer is delivery-kickoff, which seeds the logs it stewards, and its downstream consumer is acceptance-testing, which feeds it defects and test progress once Validate starts. Status does not re-plan: the plan, the baseline, and the gates stay where they were signed, and what this skill produces is the honest record of movement against them.

- Does not author change orders or scope language. Candidates route to authorized humans for a contractual decision; the contract scope and obligation review mode in `statement-of-work` reviews the resulting terms.
- Does not run kickoff, seed the charter, or create the governance logs from scratch on its own initiative. That is `delivery-kickoff`; this skill stewards what kickoff seeded.
- Does not track UAT execution or defects. That is `acceptance-testing`.
- Does not grade backlog readiness or plan sprints. `backlog-refinement` and `sprint-planning` do, and they propose RAID entries (dependencies, risks) that this skill records with stable IDs under `references/log-stewardship.md`. A plan or readiness report that cites a RAID ID not in the log fails their gates, so record proposals before they are cited.
- Does not price, estimate hours, or compute burn from anything but a named source. The Pricing System and timesheets own the numbers.
- Does not produce client-facing proposals or sales artifacts.

## Files

- `references/status-report-spec.md` : section-by-section spec for the weekly status, with worked line examples.
- `references/log-stewardship.md` : RAID and decision log rules, the stable ID convention, entry and closure formats.
- `references/scope-drift-protocol.md` : detection protocol, trigger classification, the evidence-trail format for a candidate.
- `assets/weekly-status-template.md` : the report template the model fills. Placeholders are `{{LIKE_THIS}}`; the gate fails on any that survive.
- `scripts/status_check.py` : the deterministic gate. Stdlib only.
- `scripts/status_check_selftest.py` : passing and failing fixtures; run it after any change to the gate.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and
not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply writing-integrity to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,
   footer.
3. Run quality-gate before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

  1. Logs: a dependency entry (D-0NN, client to confirm whether NetSuite is a requirement or a wish, owner and resolve-by date) and, if a human decided anything in the room, a decision entry. No decision entry for the ask itself; nobody decided anything yet.
  2. Drift: a candidate block in the scope-drift section. Trigger class hard, the ask quoted verbatim with speaker and date, the SOW integration clause cited by section and quoted, at least one evidence line, routed to Program Lead and CSE.
  3. Status: the candidate appears in the flags section as well as the scope-drift section, because it needs a decision. It reappears every period until a decision lands and gets a D-0NN.

The wrong outputs, for contrast: logging it as an action item for the team (silent absorption), deciding it is out of scope in the report (a human call), or drafting the change order (authorized humans own contractual changes; the contract scope and obligation review mode in statement-of-work reviews the resulting terms).

State discipline

  • Record IDs and quote totals are not durable anchors across sandbox refreshes. Stamp the report with its source objects and as-of dates: the SOW identifier and signed date, the timesheet export date, the transcript dates, the previous status filename.
  • Truth hierarchy when sources disagree: signed SOW and its exhibits > governance logs > previous status file > chat context > memory. A conflict between them is flagged in the report, never silently resolved; show both and say which the report uses and why.
  • Never hand-patch an issued report. Fix the log or the source, regenerate, and reissue with a new issue date; otherwise the next cadence run resurrects the error.

Running unattended

Phases 2 and 3 normally propose before appending. On a scheduled or headless run: append log entries with a clearly marked proposed status, produce the report, run the gate, and state in the flags section that the proposed entries and any drift candidates await human review. Never record a decision nobody made, never close a RAID item unattended, and never issue the report to the client without a human in the loop; leave it as a draft for the Program Lead.

Phase 6: land it

If any lifecycle gate moved this period, verify the engagement's DELIVERY-STATE.md reflects it (status, date, append-only log line) per delivery-suite's references/delivery-state-spec.md; a stale state file is a flag in the report.

Deliver the report, and commit the report plus the updated logs to the engagement folder so the next cadence run can find them; the previous-status reconciliation in Phase 0 depends on this. Name the report with the period end date (status-2026-08-08.md) so ordering is unambiguous. Close with the user on: the flags, any change-order candidates raised, and the biggest judgment call of the period argued from both sides.

Status reports are issued, not signed. Drift flags are proposals for a human decision.

Durable output

The status report is the run's durable Markdown record and follows _shared/output-contract.md: the period, the sources used, the counts, the flags, and the change-order candidates all live in the file, named by period end date and committed to the engagement folder. A run that stops before issuing still leaves a record of what was checked and what blocked it. Deliver or link the file; never just say it was written.

When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: (1) the narrative accomplishments detail, keep the outcome bullets; (2) upcoming-period detail beyond the next gate; (3) artifact-register updates beyond what moved. Never cut: the period header, log stewardship for decisions and new risks, the scope-drift section, sourcing, or the gate.

Boundaries

In the delivery chain (SOW, then s2d-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then UAT, then cutover-closeout), this skill's upstream producer is delivery-kickoff, which seeds the logs it stewards, and its downstream consumer is acceptance-testing, which feeds it defects and test progress once Validate starts. Status does not re-plan: the plan, the baseline, and the gates stay where they were signed, and what this skill produces is the honest record of movement against them.

  • Does not author change orders or scope language. Candidates route to authorized humans for a contractual decision; the contract scope and obligation review mode in statement-of-work reviews the resulting terms.
  • Does not run kickoff, seed the charter, or create the governance logs from scratch on its own initiative. That is delivery-kickoff; this skill stewards what kickoff seeded.
  • Does not track UAT execution or defects. That is acceptance-testing.
  • Does not grade backlog readiness or plan sprints. backlog-refinement and sprint-planning do, and they propose RAID entries (dependencies, risks) that this skill records with stable IDs under references/log-stewardship.md. A plan or readiness report that cites a RAID ID not in the log fails their gates, so record proposals before they are cited.
  • Does not price, estimate hours, or compute burn from anything but a named source. The Pricing System and timesheets own the numbers.
  • Does not produce client-facing proposals or sales artifacts.

Files

  • references/status-report-spec.md : section-by-section spec for the weekly status, with worked line examples.
  • references/log-stewardship.md : RAID and decision log rules, the stable ID convention, entry and closure formats.
  • references/scope-drift-protocol.md : detection protocol, trigger classification, the evidence-trail format for a candidate.
  • assets/weekly-status-template.md : the report template the model fills. Placeholders are {{LIKE_THIS}}; the gate fails on any that survive.
  • scripts/status_check.py : the deterministic gate. Stdlib only.
  • scripts/status_check_selftest.py : passing and failing fixtures; run it after any change to the gate.

Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in release-gate.md (../_shared/release-gate.md).

  1. Apply writing-integrity to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For

a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.

  1. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,

footer.

  1. Run quality-gate before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.
skills.excerptHtml:
Keep the engagement record honest, week after week. Three jobs, always together: issue the status report from the record, steward the RAID and decision logs so nothing is re-litigated, and compare observed work against the SOW scope baseline so drift is flagged with evidence before it eats margin. Undocumented decisions cause the same conversation twice; unflagged drift becomes a change order handled reactively or, worse, absorbed silently.

Use the invocation actually configured for the engagement. A reporting cadence does not establish an automatic trigger; require configuration and run evidence before reporting that a scheduled or event-driven update occurred. Every run states exactly what period it covers and reconciles against the previous status file on disk, not against memory of a prior session.

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location, and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead, and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations. Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

skills.markdown:
---
name: delivery-suite
description: 'Orchestrates the delivery half of the Estate sell-to-deliver lifecycle from signed SOW through hypercare closeout. It owns the Handoff-through-closeout stage map and its human gates. Named skills own the artifacts and the per-engagement DELIVERY-STATE.md records their state. Use when a request concerns a live delivery engagement and the owning skill is not obvious. Do not use for pre-signature work; route directly to the named sales artifact owner.'
---


# Estate delivery suite

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../writing-integrity/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

The coordinator for delivery engagements after signature. It identifies the current stage, what gate
comes next, and which skill does the work. Content decisions stay with the skill
that owns each artifact. This file stays thin on purpose: the moment it starts
describing how to build a charter or a test script, it is competing with the
owner, and instruction competition is the defect the house model exists to kill.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Where the files are

`scripts/` holds `plan.py` and its selftest with fixtures. `references/` holds
`stage-map.md` (the full stage, gate, and owner table plus routing edge cases and
the known-gaps register) and `delivery-state-spec.md` (the DELIVERY-STATE.md
format). Read `stage-map.md` before routing anything unusual; the table below is
the compact form.

## The lifecycle is eight ordered steps

Handoff (pre-stage), then 01 Mobilize, 02 Analyze, 03 Design, 04 Build,
05 Validate, 06 Deploy, and the closeout loop inside 06. Each exits through a
named gate, several co-signed by the client. Gates are exit conditions held by
humans; skills draft, humans approve and sign. Preserve existing stage IDs in an engagement record. Apply the gates required
by its accepted project plan; never mark one passed without its acceptance record.

## Who owns what

Read the [stage model](references/stages.json) for the current task owners and
exit gates. The planner reads that same model. Read [the stage guide](references/stage-map.md)
for stage work and routing exceptions. Mobilization uses delivery-kickoff;
validation uses acceptance-testing. Delivery-status maintains the reporting
cadence and flags potential scope changes.

Use the project's authorized implementation workflow for Build. Keep its actual
build evidence distinct from acceptance. Apply writing-integrity to all authored
prose; use the shared brand runtime for styled artifacts. The executed agreement
and accepted changes govern commitments. This router does not approve a price.

## How to route a request

1. **Find the engagement and its state file.** `DELIVERY-STATE.md` at the
   engagement folder root. Truth hierarchy: executed SOW/quote > artifact files >
   state file > memory > chat. If the state file is missing, do not guess from
   chat: locate the hard evidence (signed SOW? accepted brief? signed charter?
   co-signed requirements?) and write the state file from it per
   `references/delivery-state-spec.md` before routing.
2. **Run the planner.** Never assemble the plan by hand.

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/plan.py path/to/DELIVERY-STATE.md
   ```

   It prints where the engagement is, the next gate and who holds it, the
   ordered remaining stages with their owning skills, and findings (out-of-order
   gates, a stage line that disagrees with the gate ledger, unparseable entries).
   Report the position and every finding; do not narrate the run. `--json` gives
   the machine contract; the text default is the one to use.
3. **State the position plainly to the user.** Stage, next gate, gate holder.
   If the user's request belongs to a different stage than the engagement is in,
   say so before routing; building ahead of an unpassed gate gets rebuilt.
4. **Hand off to the owning skill by name**, with the engagement folder, the
   state file path, and the specific artifact asked for. This suite does not
   build the artifact, review it, or restate the owner's method.
5. **Verify the state file moved.** Whichever skill closes a gate updates
   DELIVERY-STATE.md in the same session (gate status with date, artifact path,
   append-only log line). When routing next, check the update happened; a stale
   state file makes every later plan wrong.

## Durable output

This suite produces no business artifact; those belong to the specialists it
routes to. What it does leave, per `_shared/output-contract.md`, is the run's
own Markdown record: the planner output (position, next gate, remaining
stages, findings), the routing decision made, and any state-file corrections,
alongside the updated DELIVERY-STATE.md itself. Deliver or link the record;
never just say it was written.

## Gate discipline

- A gate passes when the signed or accepted artifact exists, not when the work
  feels done. The planner treats an undated pass as suspect; so should you.
- Reopening a passed gate is scope drift first: log it through
  `delivery-status` and assess the change-order candidate before any
  rework starts.
- Apply the Go-Live Acceptance mechanism in the executed agreement. Use a
  deemed-acceptance clock only when the agreement actually contains one;
  otherwise obtain its specified acceptance evidence. `cutover-closeout` owns
  that check. This suite does not close the gate without that evidence.
- A blocked gate is a finding with an owner and a resolve-by date in the state
  file's open decisions, never a reason to route around the gate.

## Check current capabilities and gaps

Inspect the caller's actual comparables library, authorized automation, and
approval records before reporting a gap. If prior-deal evidence is unavailable,
record that limit rather than inventing a comparison. Do not promise automatic

The coordinator for delivery engagements after signature. It identifies the current stage, what gate comes next, and which skill does the work. Content decisions stay with the skill that owns each artifact. This file stays thin on purpose: the moment it starts describing how to build a charter or a test script, it is competing with the owner, and instruction competition is the defect the house model exists to kill.

Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location, and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead, and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations. Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

Where the files are

scripts/ holds plan.py and its selftest with fixtures. references/ holds stage-map.md (the full stage, gate, and owner table plus routing edge cases and the known-gaps register) and delivery-state-spec.md (the DELIVERY-STATE.md format). Read stage-map.md before routing anything unusual; the table below is the compact form.

The lifecycle is eight ordered steps

Handoff (pre-stage), then 01 Mobilize, 02 Analyze, 03 Design, 04 Build, 05 Validate, 06 Deploy, and the closeout loop inside 06. Each exits through a named gate, several co-signed by the client. Gates are exit conditions held by humans; skills draft, humans approve and sign. Preserve existing stage IDs in an engagement record. Apply the gates required by its accepted project plan; never mark one passed without its acceptance record.

Who owns what

Read the stage model (references/stages.json) for the current task owners and exit gates. The planner reads that same model. Read the stage guide (references/stage-map.md) for stage work and routing exceptions. Mobilization uses delivery-kickoff; validation uses acceptance-testing. Delivery-status maintains the reporting cadence and flags potential scope changes.

Use the project's authorized implementation workflow for Build. Keep its actual build evidence distinct from acceptance. Apply writing-integrity to all authored prose; use the shared brand runtime for styled artifacts. The executed agreement and accepted changes govern commitments. This router does not approve a price.

How to route a request

  1. Find the engagement and its state file. DELIVERY-STATE.md at the

engagement folder root. Truth hierarchy: executed SOW/quote > artifact files > state file > memory > chat. If the state file is missing, do not guess from chat: locate the hard evidence (signed SOW? accepted brief? signed charter? co-signed requirements?) and write the state file from it per references/delivery-state-spec.md before routing.

  1. Run the planner. Never assemble the plan by hand.
   python3 scripts/plan.py path/to/DELIVERY-STATE.md
   ```

It prints where the engagement is, the next gate and who holds it, the
   ordered remaining stages with their owning skills, and findings (out-of-order
   gates, a stage line that disagrees with the gate ledger, unparseable entries).
   Report the position and every finding; do not narrate the run. `--json` gives
   the machine contract; the text default is the one to use.
3. **State the position plainly to the user.** Stage, next gate, gate holder.
   If the user's request belongs to a different stage than the engagement is in,
   say so before routing; building ahead of an unpassed gate gets rebuilt.
4. **Hand off to the owning skill by name**, with the engagement folder, the
   state file path, and the specific artifact asked for. This suite does not
   build the artifact, review it, or restate the owner's method.
5. **Verify the state file moved.** Whichever skill closes a gate updates
   DELIVERY-STATE.md in the same session (gate status with date, artifact path,
   append-only log line). When routing next, check the update happened; a stale
   state file makes every later plan wrong.

This suite produces no business artifact; those belong to the specialists it
routes to. What it does leave, per `_shared/output-contract.md`, is the run's
own Markdown record: the planner output (position, next gate, remaining

skills.markdown:
---
name: discovery-brief
description: 'Maintain the discovery record for a pursuit: supported facts and ranked open questions tied to the scope they unblock. Use to prepare discovery content, identify questions that affect scope or price, ingest a post-call transcript, close answered questions, log decisions, or propose scope revisions. Route company research and a packaged call brief to call-prep, scope and pricing changes to scoping-agent, and signed-engagement requirements to requirements-capture.'
---


# Discovery brief

## Caller context and source boundary

Use only the current task's supplied or explicitly authorized account, project sources and destinations. Resolve record names such as `client.profile` within that confirmed context; they are logical slots, not a default personal store. Connector availability alone does not authorize searching another account. Organization-specific pricing, capability catalogs, approval roles and policies must be supplied or confirmed; absent material context remains an explicit gap. Keep reusable package files immutable during a client task and save client records outside them. Never populate an example with private source material.


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../prose-pass/references/registers/readout-brief.md).**

This skill owns `opportunity.discovery`. It maintains a two-column ledger before
and after each pursuit discovery session. `call-prep` uses that ledger to package
one upcoming call. `scoping-agent` decides whether proposed findings change
scope or price.

## The ledger

Build the ledger before writing a brief. Detailed fields and examples are in
[`ledger-spec.md`](references/ledger-spec.md).

**Column A: supported knowledge.** Each atomic claim carries a source ID, source
date, as-of date, and Confirmed or Inferred status. Confirmed needs authoritative
evidence. Inferred states its basis. A searched-for fact that remains absent
becomes a Column B question.

**Column B: open questions.** Write each question as it should be asked. Record
what was searched, the scope line or capability it unblocks, and its impact:

- High blocks sizing, creates a wide cost range, or gates a phase.
- Medium changes effort inside a workstream that can still be sized.
- Low refines the estimate at the margin.

Ask higher-impact questions first. For equal impact, prioritize the question
that gates other work. Remove questions that cannot change scope, effort, price,
or a delivery decision. An unresolved item carries `do not size until Q-nn` in
the relevant scope row.

## Inspection and persistence state

Record only sources actually inspected. If the input summarizes what “transcript line N says,” cite the supplied summary of line N; do not claim that the transcript itself was searched. A search field can say “supplied summary only; full transcript unavailable.” An excerpt or summary is not a full-transcript search; record its exact available lines and keep the missing source as a retrieval gap. An attributed statement establishes what that speaker said, not independently verified authority for sizing or approval. Narrow a question when the available evidence answers only part of it.

When no write occurred, present an unapplied ledger patch. If a write was attempted but its result or readback is missing, report persistence as unverified or unknown and inspect the destination before retrying; do not call that patch unapplied. Label evidence registration, refresh and validation as proposed actions unless they ran. Preserve supplied human text exactly; if the human block is absent, retain a placeholder for its unchanged contents rather than inventing a note or claiming it was checked.

## Evidence and commercial rules

Run `evidence-core` before building the ledger. Register sources in
`evidence.sources` and claims in `evidence.claims`. Generated artifacts and
worked examples have no evidence authority. A load-bearing Insufficient result
produces a discovery readiness gap memo and stops the full brief.

Every commercial number comes from an approved quote or explicit user-supplied
source. This skill can identify an unsized line. It cannot create hours, rates,
fees, or totals.

## Prepare discovery

1. Resolve the client and opportunity. Confirm the session, attendees, purpose,
   available time, opportunity ID, and quote identifier when one exists.
2. Read `client.front_door`, `client.profile`, `opportunity.front_door`,
   `opportunity.discovery`, and the relevant evidence index.
3. Read authoritative internal sources before asking a person. Include the RFP,
   capability scoring, CRM record, workshop transcripts, client documents, and
   approved commercial records that are available.
4. Build Column A from governed claims. Preserve conflicts.
5. Build and rank Column B from the remaining gaps. Tie every question to a
   named scope line or decision.
6. Validate the ledger before projecting the brief.

Use the section catalog in
[`section-catalog.md`](references/section-catalog.md) for the brief. The ranked
unknowns remain its spine. Add a flex section only when the ledger supports it.

## Ingest the call

Use `transcript-ingestion` to preserve and normalize the raw source when it is
installed. Follow
[`post-call-ingestion.md`](references/post-call-ingestion.md):

1. Resolve the speaker-labeled transcript by stable context identity.
2. Walk each open question. Move a supported answer to Column A; narrow a partial
   answer; retain an unanswered question.
3. Extract new facts and decisions with transcript locations.
4. Send proposed claims through `evidence-core`.
5. Write supported findings to `opportunity.discovery`. Update `client.profile`
   only for durable client facts.
6. Send proposed scope changes to `scoping-agent` for confirmation.
7. Re-rank the remaining questions and refresh the brief.

Never close a question without transcript evidence. Preserve human-authored
blocks between `<!-- human -->` and `<!-- /human -->`. When revising a complete
Pursuit Brief, run call-prep's before-and-after preservation check.

## Validate and release

```bash
python3 scripts/check_brief.py ledger.json
```

The gate checks source tokens, valid ranks, named scope lines, rank order,
unknown placement, and object structure. An empty JSON open-question list passes only when discovery_complete is explicitly true; punctuation alone does not fail this evidence gate. Exit 0 passes. A nonzero result
blocks release.

Apply `writing-integrity` to the brief and `brand-renderer` on any branded surface. Apply
`quality-gate` before final delivery. The shared sequence is in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

## Failure behavior

- Unavailable sources remain retrieval gaps; they do not prove absence.
- A question already answered by the record is removed from Column B.
- A priced unresolved item fails the brief.
- A source conflict stays visible until an authorized owner resolves it.
- A headless run may build and gate the ledger. It cannot invent an answer,
  approve scope, or close a client decision.
- Read-only Hub access returns exact patches and `patch-returned`.

## Durable result

Return the ledger, projected brief, or readiness gap memo under
[`output-contract.md`](../_shared/output-contract.md). Name the client and
opportunity, sources searched, records read, top open questions, gate result,
proposed scope changes, and persistence state.

## Files

- `references/ledger-spec.md`: Column A and B formats.
- `references/section-catalog.md`: brief sections and retrieval targets.
- `references/post-call-ingestion.md`: transcript-to-ledger protocol.
- `scripts/check_brief.py`: Markdown and JSON gate.
- `scripts/check_brief_selftest.py`: passing and failing fixtures.

capability scoring, CRM record, workshop transcripts, client documents, and approved commercial records that are available.

  1. Build Column A from governed claims. Preserve conflicts.
  2. Build and rank Column B from the remaining gaps. Tie every question to a

named scope line or decision.

  1. Validate the ledger before projecting the brief.

Use the section catalog in section-catalog.md (references/section-catalog.md) for the brief. The ranked unknowns remain its spine. Add a flex section only when the ledger supports it.

Ingest the call

Use transcript-ingestion to preserve and normalize the raw source when it is installed. Follow post-call-ingestion.md (references/post-call-ingestion.md):

  1. Resolve the speaker-labeled transcript by stable context identity.
  2. Walk each open question. Move a supported answer to Column A; narrow a partial

answer; retain an unanswered question.

  1. Extract new facts and decisions with transcript locations.
  2. Send proposed claims through evidence-core.
  3. Write supported findings to opportunity.discovery. Update client.profile

only for durable client facts.

  1. Send proposed scope changes to scoping-agent for confirmation.
  2. Re-rank the remaining questions and refresh the brief.

Never close a question without transcript evidence. Preserve human-authored blocks between ` and `. When revising a complete Pursuit Brief, run call-prep's before-and-after preservation check.

Validate and release

python3 scripts/check_brief.py ledger.json

The gate checks source tokens, valid ranks, named scope lines, rank order, unknown placement, and object structure. An empty JSON open-question list passes only when discovery_complete is explicitly true; punctuation alone does not fail this evidence gate. Exit 0 passes. A nonzero result blocks release.

Apply writing-integrity to the brief and brand-renderer on any branded surface. Apply quality-gate before final delivery. The shared sequence is in release-gate.md (../_shared/release-gate.md).

Failure behavior

  • Unavailable sources remain retrieval gaps; they do not prove absence.
  • A question already answered by the record is removed from Column B.
  • A priced unresolved item fails the brief.
  • A source conflict stays visible until an authorized owner resolves it.
  • A headless run may build and gate the ledger. It cannot invent an answer,

approve scope, or close a client decision.

  • Read-only Hub access returns exact patches and patch-returned.

Durable result

Return the ledger, projected brief, or readiness gap memo under output-contract.md (../_shared/output-contract.md). Name the client and opportunity, sources searched, records read, top open questions, gate result, proposed scope changes, and persistence state.

Files

  • references/ledger-spec.md: Column A and B formats.
  • references/section-catalog.md: brief sections and retrieval targets.
  • references/post-call-ingestion.md: transcript-to-ledger protocol.
  • scripts/check_brief.py: Markdown and JSON gate.
  • scripts/check_brief_selftest.py: passing and failing fixtures.

---
name: discovery-synthesis
description: 'Synthesize supplied discovery calls, interview notes, transcripts or Granola and Fathom exports into sourced findings: job statements, pain points with severity, exact verbatims, speaker-attributed insights, a TL;DR, open questions and next steps. Use when the user shares meeting content and asks what was learned, to pull insights from a transcript, map pain points or extract JTBDs. For the deal discovery record, ranked ledger or open questions, select the maintain pursuit findings mode and read discovery-brief.'
---


# Discovery Synthesis

## Caller context and source boundary

Use only the current task's supplied or explicitly authorized account, project sources and destinations. Resolve record names such as `client.profile` within that confirmed context; they are logical slots, not a default personal store. Connector availability alone does not authorize searching another account. Organization-specific pricing, capability catalogs, approval roles and policies must be supplied or confirmed; absent material context remains an explicit gap. Keep reusable package files immutable during a client task and save client records outside them. Never populate an example with private source material.


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../prose-pass/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Turn discovery calls into sourced research findings for the current project. Use its industry, participants and terminology.

## Boundary with the discovery brief

This skill is the synthesis pass: raw call content in, sourced findings out. The
maintain pursuit findings mode uses [discovery-brief](../discovery-brief/SKILL.md),
which owns the deal's ranked two-column ledger, its open questions and the feed
into the pursuit brief. Select that complete workflow when the request is to
update the deal's structured record or ask what is still unknown about the
account. A synthesis can supply new findings to that ledger; it does not replace
it. The portable Discovery package embeds both workflows; no separate installation
is needed for the ledger mode.

## Supported input types

| Input type | How to handle |
|---|---|
| Pasted text or typed notes | Use directly |
| Uploaded .txt or .md | Read the file contents |
| Uploaded .docx | Use the `docx` skill to extract text first. Find it in your available skills; do not assume a path. |
| Uploaded .pdf | Use the `pdf` skill to extract text first. Find it in your available skills; do not assume a path. |
| Granola transcript | Pull it through the Granola MCP connector (`get_meeting_transcript`, `list_meetings`). There is no Granola skill. |
| Fathom transcript | Ask the user to paste or export the transcript |
| Audio or video file | Direct audio processing is not supported. Ask for a transcript or a Granola or Fathom export. |

## Workflow

1. Confirm the client, meeting type, who attended on each side and any known focus area. Infer what the content makes obvious and ask once for the rest. When the user wants speed, proceed and state the assumptions at the top.
2. Read the supplied content completely. A summary is secondary evidence and cannot become a verbatim transcript. Keep uncertain speaker labels uncertain.
3. Separate client voices from consulting-team voices. Client statements are the research signal; consultant questions are context.
4. Record each finding with its source location and speaker role. Keep one person's observation distinct from a pattern several people share, and retain meaningful dissent.
5. Rate severity from the source wording. Blocking, repeated or urgent statements are high. Frustration without a block is medium. A single vague mention is low. State the reason for each rating.
6. Write the output in the format and length the user asked for. Without a narrower request, cover the sections below in plain headings.
7. Run the release gate.

## What the synthesis covers

The TL;DR gives the core problem, the most urgent pain and the largest opportunity in two to four sentences, with the session details it draws on.

Job statements use *When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome].* Write a job statement only where the source shows the outcome the client wants. Cite the signal and the speaker role for each one. `jtbd-framing` holds the bar these statements must meet.

Pain points state what was said in plain language, with severity, frequency, evidence and speaker role. Describe the problem; recommendations belong elsewhere.

Opportunity areas are the team's inference from the pain points and job statements. Label them as proposed and link each one to the findings it rests on.

Verbatims are exact quotations from client speakers. Preserve the exact words and grammar of a quote with its speaker and timestamp or source location. Never invent a representative quote. Label a paraphrase as a paraphrase outside quotation marks. Select only useful quotes present in the source, even when there are few. Include a consultant quote only when it provoked a revealing client response.

Speaker-attributed insights describe each distinct client voice: apparent priorities, key concerns and influence signals, each tied to what the person said.

Open questions and next steps name what the session left unconfirmed, the follow-up that would answer it and the responsible project role when the source identifies one; otherwise leave ownership open. Send questions that belong to the deal record to the maintain pursuit findings mode.

Gaps and assumptions list information the analysis needed but the source did not contain. When the transcript is thin, say so instead of padding with weak inferences.

## Output delivery

Render the synthesis in Markdown in chat. Save a Markdown file in the project's existing output folder when files can be saved; otherwise provide the complete content in chat. When the user asks for a Word document, use the `docx` skill from your available skills and save it beside the Markdown file. Link saved files through the host's supported file-link mechanism.

A local save does not upload a file to NotebookLM or a Claude Project. Upload only to an authorized destination the user requests, and read back the saved record before claiming it is available there. When the project has a confirmed assessment framework, connect opportunity areas to it.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply writing-integrity to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run quality-gate before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

# DevOps Center Promotion

Guides validation, conditional preparation, combination, promotion, and completion in DevOps Center. Retain each structured command response and its operation identifier. A successful command start does not prove deployment completion, and retry safety must be checked for the particular operation.

## Work without an org

The bundled capability inspector and stage router work locally with Python 3. They do not require jq. With a saved plugin manifest, `python3 scripts/preflight.py --manifest plugin.json` makes no Salesforce CLI call; without that flag it only runs local `sf plugins inspect`. Add `--require-combine` when the proposed workflow combines work items. The JSON receipt distinguishes local capabilities from org or promotion verification.

`python3 scripts/promotion-route.py --current-stage-id "" --target-stage-id FIRST --first-stage-id FIRST` exercises the first-stage route without a connection. Use synthetic inputs for practice and retain their outputs as local checks. A missing org stops the live phases below; it does not authorize using a cached alias or changing the machine default. Do not claim deployment acceptance from these local tools.

## Scope

  - **In scope**: Validate plugin capabilities and promotion preconditions, conditionally prepare a work item, recover a stale WI branch, combine work items that share metadata into one promotion, promote one or more work items or an entire source stage to a target stage, and complete the promotion
  - **Out of scope**: Work item creation/status updates (use `dx-devops-work-item-manage`), polling an existing promotion's status, pipeline or project setup (separate skills)

---

## Required Inputs

Gather or infer before proceeding:

- **Promotion target**: one or more specific work items, or all approved work items in a source stage
- **Target stage ID**: `--target-stage-id`, required for validate, combine, promote, complete, and for prepare only when prepare is routed
- **Work item ID(s)** or **source stage ID** — depending on the promotion target. `sf devops promote` takes `--work-item-id` (repeatable) XOR `--stage-id`
- **For combined promotion**: a parent work item ID and one or more child work item IDs that share metadata
- **Target org**: an explicitly authorized `--target-org <alias>` for this operation; never infer it from a machine default or cached alias.

Defaults unless specified:
- Output format: `--json` for headless consumption
- Test level: omit `--test-level` for development-stage deploys (defaults to `NoTestRun`); use `RunLocalTests` for production-stage deploys with Apex

If the user gives a clear request ("promote work item 1fkxx… to stage 1QVxx…", "promote the QA stage to UAT", "combine these work items and promote"), proceed once you have the required IDs.

---

## Workflow

All operations use `sf devops` CLI commands with `--json` output. Capability preflight runs before org access, and promotion validation always runs before mutation. All promotion commands are keyed on **record IDs**, not work item names. Resolve names to IDs first if needed.

### Phase 0 — Plugin and capability preflight

1. **Run the shipped preflight before starting:**
   ```bash
   scripts/preflight.sh
   ```
   - Require `@salesforce/plugin-devops-center >=2.0.0`; inspect the installed version and capabilities before use. The historical examples used 2.2.0; that is not a current deployment-verification claim.
   - Inspect the plugin manifest, not only version text. Require `devops:promotion:validate`, `devops:promote`, `devops:work-item:prepare`, `devops:promotion:complete`, and the promote `skip-validation` flag. Add `--require-combine` to require `devops:work-item:combine` before a combined promotion.
   - If the plugin is missing, obsolete, invalid, or lacks a capability, STOP with the exact failed check and an install/upgrade instruction. Do not substitute older or guessed commands.

### Phase 1 — Authenticate and Validate

2. **Verify org authentication** before any operation:
   ```bash
   sf org display --target-org <confirmed-alias> --json
   ```
   - If it fails, instruct the user to run `sf org login web --alias <confirmed-alias>`
   - Pass the confirmed `--target-org <alias>` on every command. A configured default is not confirmation of the target.

3. **Run the mandatory validate step**. This is non-negotiable and always runs before prepare/combine/promote. `sf devops promotion validate` requires the target stage (`-t/--target-stage-id`) and one or more `-i/--work-item-id`:
   ```bash
   # Capture the output — Phase 2 derives the combine decision from it deterministically.
   VALIDATE_JSON=$(sf devops promotion validate --work-item-id <id> --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> --target-org <alias> --json)
   ```
   - Validates whether the work item(s) can be promoted to the target stage — checks for VCS and object-permission errors (including the associated-PR requirement) before a promotion is attempted
   - Repeat `--work-item-id` to validate multiple work items in one call
   - **Success:** `status == 0` and `.result.success == true` — proceed
   - **If validation fails** (non-zero exit; e.g. `VCS_ERROR: No pull request exists…`, with `.result.errorType`/`.result.errorDetails` set), STOP. Report the error and do not proceed. If it references metadata overlap, resolve the conflict before retrying
   - **Shared components:** when `.result.combineDetails` is non-null, the work items share metadata — validate returns the parent/child grouping and `suggestions`. This is the authoritative signal for the Phase 2 combine decision (see step 6); do not guess whether to combine — the Phase 2 script reads `.result.combineDetails` from `VALIDATE_JSON`

### Phase 2 — Prepare (and optionally Combine)

4. **Route preparation before running it:**
   ```bash
   scripts/promotion-route.sh \
     --current-stage-id "${PIPELINE_STAGE_ID:-}" \
     --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> \
     --first-stage-id <first-linked-stage-id>
   ```
   - If the development WI has no `PipelineStageId` and is entering the first linked pipeline stage, the route is `skip`. Do not call prepare. DevOps Center already owns this normal first-stage path.
   - If the WI already has a pipeline stage and is being promoted one-off to another pipeline stage, the route is `prepare`.
   - If the WI has no stage but the requested target is not the first linked stage, STOP as ambiguous. Do not guess or force preparation.
   - Resolve the first linked stage from pipeline topology and read the WI's `pipelineStageId`/`PipelineStageId` from current DevOps Center data.

5. **Prepare only when the route is `prepare`:**
   ```bash
   sf devops work-item prepare --work-item-id <id> --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> --target-org <alias> --json
   ```
   - This command is for one-off promotion between existing pipeline stages.
   - `--target-stage-id` is required and is the same target stage the work item will be promoted to.
   - Before retrying, inspect the returned status and current work-item state. Do not assume a repeated mutation is harmless.

6. **Derive combination from the saved validation response.** Save the complete Phase 1 JSON as `validation.json`; preserve the command receipt with its explicit org, target stage, work-item set, and source revision. Then run:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/combine-plan.py --validation validation.json
   ```
   The helper requires numeric status 0 and `result.success: true`. An explicit null `combineDetails` produces `combine: false`. A combine object must have one parent and a nonempty list of distinct child IDs; missing or malformed details fail. It returns a JSON `arguments` array and the validation file hash. It never calls Salesforce or claims the saved response is current.

   If `combine` is true, rerun capability preflight with `--require-combine`. Confirm that the saved validation still belongs to the exact current org, work items, target stage, and unchanged source. Supply the returned argument list to `sf devops work-item combine`, followed by the confirmed `--target-stage-id`, `--target-org`, and `--json` flags. Use a structured process argument list; never shell-evaluate JSON text. Retain the result, and promote the returned parent only after combination succeeds.

   If `combine` is false, skip combination. If the user has identified additional dependencies not represented in validation, resolve and revalidate them before mutation. Older reference examples use jq as an optional shell parser; this bundled helper provides the same decision without that dependency.

### Phase 3 — Promote

7. **Promote to the target stage** — exactly one of `--work-item-id` or `--stage-id` must be provided; `--target-stage-id` is always required. **Pass `--skip-validation` ONLY when the exact work-item set and target stage passed Phase 1 validation in the current session and neither Git nor DevOps Center state changed afterward.** Otherwise, omit the flag and let the CLI run its built-in validation:
   - Promote one or more specific work items (repeat `--work-item-id` per item; use the parent's ID for a combined promotion). Include the `--skip-validation` line ONLY if Phase 1 validate passed this session; otherwise drop that line:
     ```bash
     sf devops promote \
       --work-item-id <id> \
       --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> \
       --skip-validation \
       --target-org <alias> \
       --json
     ```
   - Or promote all approved work items from a source stage (again, include the `--skip-validation` line only if Phase 1 validate passed this session):
     ```bash
     sf devops promote \
       --stage-id <source-stage-id> \
       --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> \
       --skip-validation \
       --target-org <alias> \
       --json
     ```

When the full workflow ran sequentially this session, that validation already passed, so `--skip-validation` only eliminates a redundant re-run. But if the agent resumed mid-workflow, promotion was invoked without a preceding Phase 1 validate, or Phase 1 was not run for every work item being promoted, DO NOT pass `--skip-validation` — bypassing it there would skip validation entirely with no prior guard
   - Add `--deploy-all` to deploy all metadata in the branch rather than only changes not yet in the target stage
   - Add `--test-level RunLocalTests` (or `RunSpecifiedTests --tests <names>`) for production-stage deploys that include Apex
   - The deploy runs asynchronously — capture the returned promotion/deploy identifier from the JSON `.result`

### Phase 4 — Complete and Report

8. **Complete the promotion** to finalize — advances the work items in the target stage:
   ```bash
   sf devops promotion complete --target-stage-id <target-stage-id> --target-org <alias> --json
   ```
   - Run after the promote deploy succeeds to mark the promotion done in the target stage
   - `--target-stage-id` is required (same target stage the work items were promoted to)

9. **Report the outcome**:
   - Confirm the CLI returned status 0 for each step
   - Report the promotion/deploy identifier and note that async deploy completion is tracked separately
   - Do NOT block or busy-wait inside this skill — surface the identifier and return
   - State the promotion clearly: e.g., "Work item promotion initiated (source stage → target stage). Deploy ID: <id>. Poll this ID to confirm deploy completion, then run promotion complete."

---

## Rules / Constraints

| Constraint | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|
| Validate ALWAYS runs first | Guarantees preconditions are met before any mutation; skipping it can corrupt pipeline state |
| Plugin version and capabilities are inspected first | A CLI version can be installed yet lack required commands or flags; fail on skew instead of improvising |
| All `sf devops` commands must use `--json` | Structured output is required for headless consumption; human-readable output is unreliable to parse |
| Commands are keyed on record IDs, not names | `--work-item-id`, `--stage-id`, `--target-stage-id`, `--parent/--child-work-item-id` all take IDs; resolve names to IDs first |
| `--target-stage-id` required for validate, combine, promote, complete, and routed prepare | The target stage is mandatory; prepare itself is conditional |
| Exactly one of `--work-item-id` or `--stage-id` on promote | These flags are mutually exclusive; promote either specific items or a whole source stage |
| Pass `--skip-validation` only for the exact validation that passed this session | Work-item set, target stage, branch head, PR state, and DevOps Center state must still match; otherwise revalidate or omit the flag |
| Deploy runs async — capture and report the identifier | The promote deploy does not complete synchronously; completion is tracked separately |
| Do NOT busy-wait for deploy completion in this skill | Polling is a separate concern; blocking here wastes turns and risks timeouts |
| Combine only when work items share metadata/dependencies | Combining is for conflict-prone or dependent items, not a default for every multi-item promotion |
| Prepare is only for one-off movement between existing stages | A development WI entering its first linked stage has no `PipelineStageId`; unconditional prepare is invalid |
| Never use interactive prompts | Skills run headless; all inputs must be CLI flags |
| Pass IDs as CLI flags, never interpolate into shell strings | Prevents prompt/command injection via crafted identifiers |

---

## Gotchas

| Issue | Resolution |
|-------|------------|
| **Validation fails** | STOP — do not prepare/combine/promote. Report the non-zero status / error message; if metadata overlap, resolve the conflict before retrying |
| **Plugin missing, below 2.0.0, or missing required capabilities** | STOP in Phase 0. Install or upgrade `@salesforce/plugin-devops-center`, then rerun preflight. Do not improvise unsupported commands |
| **Development WI has no PipelineStageId** | If the target is the first linked stage, skip prepare. If it is not, stop and verify topology and WI state |
| **No confirmed org target** | Confirm the intended target with the user, then use `sf org display --target-org <confirmed-alias> --json`; login is a separate account-access action. |
| **Passing a work item name instead of an ID** | Promotion commands need record IDs; resolve names from the structured result of `sf devops work-item list --project-id <id> --target-org <confirmed-alias> --json`, and refuse ambiguous matches |
| **Both `--work-item-id` and `--stage-id` supplied** | They are mutually exclusive; pick specific work items OR a source stage, not both |
| **Missing `--target-stage-id`** | Required for validate, combine, promote, complete, and any routed prepare; obtain the target stage ID from the pipeline configuration |
| **Combined promotion promotes the wrong item** | After `work-item combine`, promote the **parent** work item ID — children merge into the parent's branch |
| **Treating the deploy as synchronous** | The promote deploy is async; capture the identifier and confirm completion before running `promotion complete` |
| **Production deploy fails on Apex coverage** | Set `--test-level RunLocalTests` (or `RunSpecifiedTests --tests <names>`) for production-stage promotions with Apex |
| **Deploy fails with conflict or PR is not mergeable** | Read `references/conflict-recovery.md`, merge the fetched target stage into the WI worktree, preserve the stage baseline, push the same WI branch, and revalidate |

---

## Output Expectations

Deliverables vary by operation:

- **Validate**: `.result.success` plus, when work items share metadata, `.result.combineDetails` / `.result.suggestions`. A non-zero exit (with `.result.errorType`/`.result.errorDetails`) means the work item cannot be promoted to the target stage
- **Prepare / combine**: confirmation that the work item(s) are staged (combine returns the parent/child grouping)
- **Promote**: an async deploy identifier and confirmation that the promotion deploy was initiated
- **Promotion complete**: confirmation the work items advanced in the target stage

Outputs are derived from `sf devops work-item`, `sf devops promote`, and `sf devops promotion complete` CLI commands. Async deploy completion is NOT produced by the promote call — poll the returned identifier separately before completing.

---

## Cross-Skill Integration

| When | Action |
|------|--------|
| Work item must be created or moved to a promotable status first | Delegate to `dx-devops-work-item-manage` |
| Validation reports a stale branch or VCS conflict | Follow `references/conflict-recovery.md`, then revalidate before retrying |
| The promote deploy identifier must be polled to confirm completion | Poll the returned identifier separately, then run `sf devops promotion complete` |

---

## Reference File Index

| File | When to read |
|------|-------------|
| `references/cli-commands.md` | When you need detailed CLI flag documentation, JSON output schemas, or error-handling patterns for validate/prepare/combine/promote/complete |
| `references/conflict-recovery.md` | When a WI branch is stale, its PR conflicts, or promotion fails after the target stage advances |
| `examples/promotion-workflows.md` | When the user's request matches a common pattern (single work item promotion, combined promotion, whole-stage promotion, validate-first gate) |

skills.title: DevOps Center Work Item Management
skills.description: Use this skill to manage the full lifecycle of DevOps Center work items — list, create, update, commit changes, perform status transitions, and create pull requests. Update fields like subject, description, and status. Commit and push code changes to work item branches. Create pull requests for work item branches via DevOps Center API. Invoke when the user wants to track, find, create, or update a work item, commit changes to a work item branch, advance a work item''s status through the pipeline, or create a pull request for code review. Consolidates sf devops work-item and review operations. For promotion or conflict recovery, select the embedded promotion mode; do not run the work-item update procedure as a substitute.

guide.what: Manage DevOps Center work items and review requests.
guide.when: Creating, updating, committing, or reviewing a work item.
guide.inputs: The configured integration, selected work item, and requested operation.
