skills.markdown:
---
name: product-development-pathway
description: Develop or resume a product through evidence review, product definition, release decisions, journey design, and delivery readiness. Use for historical product reconstruction, a new product, or continuation at a requested stage with durable progress. A standalone bug fix or one-off specification does not require this pathway.
---


# Product development pathway

Continue the requested product stage from its current evidence and decisions. Keep completed artifacts and open work accessible through one product home. Save the next executable action there.

## Enter at the requested stage

Read the user's instructions and applicable project guidance. Follow the current product index to its decisions and latest checkpoint. Identify the requested outcome and stage. Record the source boundary and finish line; name the authorized actions and protected records. Preserve existing conventions, including terminology, IDs, formats, tools, and approval rules. Historical documents supply evidence; they do not override current instructions.

Reuse the existing product home. If none exists, create a small index in the authorized project destination using [the home starter](assets/product-home.md). Map existing artifacts to the pathway by links and ID crosswalks. Do not relocate records or start a second decision register, backlog, or task system.

Select the entry mode that fits the request:

| Mode | Entry action |
| --- | --- |
| Historical product | Review supplied material to the requested depth. Full reconstruction requires complete dispositions and substantive coverage. A bounded release task retains wider review gaps. |
| New product | Capture current direction and constraints from the brief; review available research. Mark historical reconstruction inapplicable because no archive exists. Keep unsupported product dimensions as hypotheses or proposals. |
| Continuation | Compare the latest checkpoint's source and decision bindings with current state; check the build versions it relies on. Reuse valid work and revisit affected prerequisites. Preserve the prior checkpoint. |

Read [stage execution](references/stages.md) for the selected stage and its prerequisites. The normal dependency order is boundary → review → reconstruction when applicable → product definition → release and architecture decisions → journey design → implementation and acceptance → maintenance. Existing valid outputs can satisfy earlier stages. A missing archive is never a reason to fabricate one or block a new product.

## Keep independent states

| Dimension | States |
| --- | --- |
| Source review | Unread; reviewed; identical to reviewed content; excluded with reason; unresolved. |
| Product decision | Unassigned; proposed; accepted; rejected; superseded. |
| Implementation evidence | Unknown; intended; static demonstration; code present; tested locally; rendered locally; deployed without verification; verified live. |

Record implementation evidence for each behavior at the layer exercised.

For each capability, distinguish **should do** (desired outcome and decision), **can do** (demonstrated behavior and limits), and **will do** (accepted commitment for a named release). Keep commitments for different releases as separate records. A reviewed source cannot accept a feature; an accepted feature cannot prove implementation; a test cannot establish demand or adoption.

Use stable IDs and exact source locators or current user decisions. Read [capture structures](references/records.md) when adding records; adapt the [record template bank](assets/record-templates.json) to existing project formats. Create only applicable records. Mark unknown information as unknown and inapplicable dimensions with a reason. Do not fill gaps with invented dates, owners, budgets, scores, or metrics.

## Choose the next action from readiness evidence

For the requested stage, record each applicable gate as `satisfied`, `blocked`, `not_assessed`, or `not_applicable`, with supporting record IDs and revisions. State separately whether the output is ready for review, ready for an authorized build, accepted for a release, or verified at a destination. A populated template or passing structural check cannot satisfy a substantive gate.

Resolve the next action in this order:

1. Reassess changed evidence that the requested result depends on.
2. Complete the nearest missing prerequisite for the requested stage; do not restart unrelated stages.
3. If a material decision blocks that work, state the exact choice and affected output. Identify the authorized decider. Continue independent supported work within scope.
4. Otherwise execute the smallest action that produces the requested output or its acceptance evidence. Name its target and required authorization. Record the expected receipt and stop condition.

Keep full product coverage separate from release readiness. A release can exclude deferred capabilities without deleting them from the catalogue. A scoped journey can be ready while wider historical review remains incomplete, unless the user made full reconstruction a prerequisite.

## Maintain the home at each work boundary

Read [continuation and change impact](references/continuity.md) when resuming, changing a baseline, or closing a work boundary. Save completed artifacts with their evidence, retain unresolved work with its dependencies, and append a checkpoint after a meaningful review, decision, design, build, or failed check. Record the exact next action in the home before ending the session. Revalidate stale claims and dependent acceptance evidence before presenting them as current.

Knowledge Hub integration is optional. Use [the hub adapter](references/knowledge-hub.md) only when the product has an authorized destination and the request includes that action. Local progress must remain usable without a hub connection. No particular hub, account, folder, or sharing boundary is part of this skill.

## Use related workflows only when needed

This skill owns stage selection, traceability, readiness, and durable product progress. If available and applicable, use `pm-spec-writing` for detailed specifications, `usability-testing` for participant research, `analytics-strategy` for measurement design, `information-architecture` for navigation, and `execution-truth` for destination verification. A product map does not require those specialized workflows automatically.

Use the project's reconciliation workflow for authorized file cleanup and its task adapter for work-item state. Use `independent-product` only for an authorized independent-product migration, and `session-handoff` for a requested session handoff. Preserve their boundaries; pathway work does not authorize cleanup, migration, outreach, deployment, or task closure. If a companion skill is absent, perform the bounded task with the evidence rules here and name any review you could not complete.

At handoff, state what changed, where it exists, who can use it, what verifies it, what remains unchanged, and the exact next action. Link the product home and latest checkpoint. Do not report proposed, local, installed, released, or live work as a later state.

skills.markdown:
---
name: prose-pass
description: Internal diagnostic and figure-preservation tools used by writing-integrity. This module supplies scanners and review records; it does not select an author voice or act as a second editor.
---

# Writing diagnostic tools

Prose Pass is retired as a standalone skill. The `prose-pass` directory is a retained internal runtime for Writing Integrity. Do not select or install it as a separate editor. Existing script paths and receipt identifiers remain compatible.

Read [writing-integrity](../writing-integrity/SKILL.md) before using these tools.
That workflow owns writing review. A confirmed personal profile supplies the
author's voice. A visual brand profile cannot impose a former employer's voice
or change a fact. These tools report detectable patterns; they do not rewrite
text or establish editorial quality.

Use the tools on every kind of authored prose, including instructions and
internal records. Keep exact source evidence and executable syntax unchanged.
Review the new wording around those spans. A file extension or audience label
does not exclude authored language from review.

## Review a saved file

```bash
python3 scripts/writing_check.py --config house.json FILE
python3 scripts/writing_check.py --config house.json --json FILE
```

The checker reads prose from supported document formats and structured text
fields. Exit 0 means it found no patterns, 1 means it found a pattern and 2 means
the check could not finish. Read its output and the complete document. Repair
the argument or sentence that caused a finding, then rerun the check.

Do not change the filename, label prose internal or put authored wording in a
quote to obtain a pass. A literal source span remains verbatim only when its
source and exact extent are identified in the internal review record. Keep
reviewing the surrounding authored text. Do not reclassify an invented claim
or an awkward sentence as captured evidence.

`prose_check.py` is a compatibility command for the same supported input path.
The older lexical engine also reports vocabulary and construction diagnostics.
Read [surface policy](references/surface-policy.md) for source-span handling.

## Review recurring patterns

Read [construction rules](references/construction-rules.md) and
[patterns](references/patterns.md) when investigating a recurring construction.
Use the applicable register for format-specific advice:

| Format | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Slides | [Deck](references/registers/deck.md) |
| Contract or proposal | [SOW and proposal](references/registers/sow-proposal.md) |
| Report or brief | [Readout](references/registers/readout-brief.md) |
| Short message | [Email and Slack](references/registers/email-slack.md) |
| Other authored text | [General](references/registers/general.md) |

Registers supply examples and format checks under writing-integrity. Preserve
required terms and confirmed voice when a legacy example uses another style.
Read headings with their body text. Remove repeated explanations and subtitles
that repeat a title. A vocabulary substitution cannot repair an empty claim.

```bash
python3 scripts/scan.py audit docs "*.md"
python3 scripts/scan.py score draft.md --json
python3 scripts/scan.py --input FILE
```

The audit command includes supported structured files and returns an error for
unsupported input. The score command reports lexical density for comparison;
its success does not establish compliance. It strips some executable spans for
that measurement. Use the complete authored-language check for release review.

Vocabulary sources remain in `scripts/rewrite_scan.py`. The generated wordlists
come from `scripts/sync_wordlists.py`; preserve their synchronization check.
Weighted lists retain their existing weights. Changes to detection require
representative positive examples and valid prose examples, not a lower budget
chosen to pass a particular draft.

## Preserve figures and meaning

Before a substantive rewrite, retain the source version. Reconcile figures:

```bash
python3 scripts/rewrite_scan.py --tie-out SOURCE REWRITE
```

An added figure needs its source. A missing source figure requires checking
whether the omission was authorized. The writing pass cannot approve a price,
scope change or commercial commitment. Use the confirmed quote or versioned
estimate and preserve its assumptions. Keep client-stated figures attributed.

Compare the finished text with its source for changed ownership and conditions.
Retain factual uncertainty and meaningful author choices. Never add a number,
quotation or anecdote to make vague writing sound specific.

## Record a required review

When the producing workflow requires a narrative review record, use:

```bash
python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py emit FILE --out receipt.json \
    --before-file SOURCE \
    --protected "commercial figures from the supplied quote" \
    --change "replaced the generic claim with the supported action"
python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py validate receipt.json
```

The record binds the file hash to the checker result and declared edits. The
validator rechecks measurable assertions and figure changes. A no-change result
needs an actual reading assessment; arbitrary edits are unnecessary. A record
does not independently establish that an editor understood the document.

Brief replies receive writing review without a receipt. Captured transcripts
remain evidence and are never rewritten for style. Newly authored descriptions
in records still receive the same writing review as any other prose.

## Select configuration

The canonical baseline is `house.json`. An explicit configuration can add
checks; it cannot disable the maintained rules. The scripts and word data ship
together and need no neighboring installed skill. See
[configuration](references/house-overlay.md) and the [tellscan rule map](references/tellscan-rule-map.md) when maintaining the diagnostic
engine. Every supported artifact still needs a complete reading against its
facts and intended reader after the commands pass.

Remove repeated explanations and subtitles that repeat a title. A vocabulary substitution cannot repair an empty claim.

python3 scripts/scan.py audit docs "*.md"
python3 scripts/scan.py score draft.md --json
python3 scripts/scan.py --input FILE

The audit command includes supported structured files and returns an error for unsupported input. The score command reports lexical density for comparison; its success does not establish compliance. It strips some executable spans for that measurement. Use the complete authored-language check for release review.

Vocabulary sources remain in scripts/rewrite_scan.py. The generated wordlists come from scripts/sync_wordlists.py; preserve their synchronization check. Weighted lists retain their existing weights. Changes to detection require representative positive examples and valid prose examples, not a lower budget chosen to pass a particular draft.

Preserve figures and meaning

Before a substantive rewrite, retain the source version. Reconcile figures:

python3 scripts/rewrite_scan.py --tie-out SOURCE REWRITE

An added figure needs its source. A missing source figure requires checking whether the omission was authorized. The writing pass cannot approve a price, scope change or commercial commitment. Use the confirmed quote or versioned estimate and preserve its assumptions. Keep client-stated figures attributed.

Compare the finished text with its source for changed ownership and conditions. Retain factual uncertainty and meaningful author choices. Never add a number, quotation or anecdote to make vague writing sound specific.

Record a required review

When the producing workflow requires a narrative review record, use:

python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py emit FILE --out receipt.json \
    --before-file SOURCE \
    --protected "commercial figures from the supplied quote" \
    --change "replaced the generic claim with the supported action"
python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py validate receipt.json

The record binds the file hash to the checker result and declared edits. The validator rechecks measurable assertions and figure changes. A no-change result needs an actual reading assessment; arbitrary edits are unnecessary. A record does not independently establish that an editor understood the document.

Brief replies receive writing review without a receipt. Captured transcripts remain evidence and are never rewritten for style. Newly authored descriptions in records still receive the same writing review as any other prose.

Select configuration

The canonical baseline is house.json. An explicit configuration can add checks; it cannot disable the maintained rules. The scripts and word data ship together and need no neighboring installed skill. See configuration (references/house-overlay.md) and the tellscan rule map (references/tellscan-rule-map.md) when maintaining the diagnostic engine. Every supported artifact still needs a complete reading against its facts and intended reader after the commands pass.

skills.markdown:
---
name: quality-gate
description: 'Select and run the required artifact release controls before any Word document, PowerPoint deck, Excel workbook, PDF, HTML page, proposal, report, email, Slack message, or decision-bearing artifact is finalized. Use for every styled or client-facing output. Requires inspected evidence from the prose review (with a prose-pass receipt for final narrative artifacts) and, for styled output, from brand-renderer plus the rendered result, not a claim that another skill was mentioned. Blocks release when a required runtime, receipt, source support, or rendered output is absent.'
---


# Quality gate

Read [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md). Open the finished artifact
and its sources before judging it. For a styled artifact, locate the
`brand-renderer` preflight report (`runtime_preflight.py --json`) and the
`brand_check.py` result. Record a missing asset or a passed control only after
the report supplies an absolute path or fails. Run an available missing check
directly; ask the user only for an input or decision the available sources
cannot supply.

## Where this sits

The producing workflow owns the artifact. This module reviews the result and
the evidence supporting it. Writing review follows writing-integrity, while
the rendering library checks the selected visual profile:

```
producing workflow -> writing-integrity -> authored prose review
producing workflow -> brand-renderer -> rendering checks
producing workflow -> quality-gate -> deliverable review
```

This skill ships no renderer and packages none. A copy of `brand-renderer` here
would make each skill the other's runtime, and one upload would ship two
renderers whose fixes could diverge. Evidence for the brand control arrives as
the caller's preflight report and `brand_check.py` output, cited by path. An
absent report is a `blocked` verdict, never a `pass`.

## Preconditions

- Identify the artifact type, audience, lifecycle stage, and decision supported.
- Confirm the artifact and its evidence record are available for review.

## Route the checks

1. Review every piece of authored prose under `writing-integrity`, including
   instructions, labels and internal records. Read the complete result and
   repair actual defects; sound prose does not need arbitrary edits. The quality
   record names this check `prose-pass`, the control `quality_gate.py` looks for.
   Run the `prose-pass` diagnostics on saved files; they report only detectable
   patterns, so a clean scan does not show that the prose was read.
   For a final narrative artifact, emit the receipt with
   `prose-pass/scripts/prose_receipt.py emit`, validate it, and put its path in
   the check's `receipt` field and the document path in `artifact.path`.
   `quality_gate.py` validates the receipt against that document's current bytes
   and reruns its prose check. A bundled gate uses the prose validator inside its
   containing package, including a shared `_runtime` folder. It refuses an
   external sibling or a validator symlink that leaves that package. Relative
   paths resolve from the quality record's directory; newly emitted receipts
   store an absolute artifact path. Regenerate an older receipt with a relative
   artifact path before final release. A blocked prose check can record the
   missing receipt while
   withholding release. Sound prose may pass unchanged only with a justified
   no-change assessment in the receipt.
2. For a styled artifact, cite `brand-renderer` evidence: the preflight report
   and the `brand_check.py` result, by path. Then render or open the actual file
   and inspect every page, slide or screen for clipping, contrast, missing
   content, wrong figures and broken controls. A color scan cannot establish
   legibility or layout. If the rendered output is missing or cannot be
   produced, the brand check is `blocked`. Brand controls identity, so an
   off-palette hex or a redrawn mark is a fail. A font substitution passes only
   when it is the selected profile's documented fallback and the record
   discloses it; any other substitution is a fail.
   Composition is content-driven, so a review flag on footer placement or
   slide layout takes a disposition and stands.
3. Apply the contract scope and obligation review mode in `statement-of-work` to SOW or contractual scope content. Retain `sow-quality` as the existing receipt control identifier.
4. Apply the producing skill's deterministic validator when one exists.
5. Reconcile claims, figures, approvals, scope, status, and go/no-go conclusions
   with their sources. Recompute totals and compare quoted numbers with the
   source. A claim whose source is missing, conflicting or too thin to support
   it is `blocked` until the source is found or the claim is removed. Marking it
   as an assumption is an alternative only for lower-risk provisional analysis,
   as in Grade. Approvals, deployment or publication status, and unsupported
   committed financial figures stay fail-closed: find the source or remove the
   claim, and never record an approval as an assumption. A generated file is not
   evidence that anyone approved,
   sent, published or deployed it. When the request included a write, check the
   destination and state the layer reached: prepared locally, committed,
   published, or verified in the destination.

Prose-pass receipts apply to narrative artifacts: briefs, proposals, SOWs,
decks, readouts, one-pagers, decision documents. Raw evidence, transcripts,
ledgers, and machine-readable files keep their exact source spans unchanged and
take accuracy checks instead of a voice rewrite. Any summary, label or comment
written around those spans is authored prose and is reviewed under item 1.

Ordinary email and Slack take a reading pass against the writing standard, no
receipt. They arrive here only once the message carries a consequential figure,
an approval, scope, a commitment, or a decision. A short message about a number
gets the same source check as a document about one.

## Grade

1. Record every check as pass, fail, blocked, or not applicable.
2. Cite the exact artifact section or validator evidence supporting the result.
3. Fail closed when any high-risk assertion lacks support.
4. Permit a lower-risk provisional draft only when gaps and limitations are explicit.

## Failure behavior

- Do not mark a check complete merely because another skill is mentioned.
- Do not claim a downstream control ran without invocation or deterministic evidence.
- Return a remediation list when release is blocked.

## Output contract

Use assertion kinds `financial_figure`, `contract_scope`, `approval_status` or `go_no_go` for those claims. Other prose can use `narrative` or an explicit `other`; unknown kinds are rejected. Do not relabel a high-risk claim to avoid its source check. For HTML, PowerPoint, Word, Excel or PDF paths, explicitly set `artifact.brand_render` to a boolean. Set it to `true` for styled output and record the rendering checks; `false` declares that styled-output review does not apply. The validator checks the declaration, not the file's visual design or the truth of a claim. Inspect the artifact to confirm both classifications.

Return a durable Markdown quality record. Include artifact identity, selected controls, performed checks, assertion evidence, release verdict, blockers, remediation, plus Knowledge Hub update status (`not_applicable` when the workflow has no hub write). The command validates record structure and the final narrative receipt. Citation and hub-status fields remain reported evidence; the command does not verify those destinations or prove that a person read the artifact. Exit 0 means the record is valid, including an honest blocked record. Require `released: true` before treating the result as release permission. Library callers pass the record directory as `base_dir` when using relative paths. Regenerate receipts after moving artifacts to another machine or folder. Reading the artifact and checking its sources remain required.

---
name: requirements-capture
description: 'Capture and structure business requirements in the Estate approved format: epics, capabilities, business needs, user stories, and Gherkin acceptance criteria, delivered as a branded two-tab Excel workbook. Use to define, write, organize, or refine requirements, to extract them from an uploaded deck, PRD, brief, spec, or transcript, or to turn a Salesforce SOW into a backlog (BA mode: analyze this SOW, SOW to backlog, Salesforce BA). Triggers on capture requirements, write user stories, define epics, requirements gathering, BRD, acceptance criteria, requirements CSV. Always read the host spreadsheet skill before generating the workbook. Grading sprint readiness is backlog-refinement.'
---


# Estate Requirements Capture

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../prose-pass/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

## Purpose

This skill guides the agent through an interactive, structured conversation to
capture business requirements in the Estate approved delivery matrix format.
The final output is a **branded Excel workbook (.xlsx)** with two tabs, ready
for client presentation and downstream use by AI agents or development teams.

## Reference files

Detailed tables live in `references/` to keep this file lean. Read the relevant
one when you reach that part of the work:

- `references/excel-workbook-format.md`: the per-column tables for both tabs,
  the default blue/white styling theme, the Epics-tab formula, and recalculation.
- `references/gherkin-and-questions.md`: Gherkin acceptance-criteria structure
  with a worked example, plus clarifying-question guidance.
- `references/jira-export-and-traceability.md`: the Source column and the
  three legitimate values for it, the gap list, and the workbook-to-Jira field
  mapping. Read it when the requirements come from a SOW or scope document, or
  when the output goes into a Jira backlog rather than staying a spreadsheet.
- `references/ba-mode-salesforce.md`: the BA mode rules for Salesforce
  engagements. Read it whenever BA mode is on (see below).

## Before Generating the Workbook

**Always read the host spreadsheet skill before writing any openpyxl code.**
Look for `xlsx`, `spreadsheets`, or the equivalent in the available skills list.
Follow its guidelines for formula construction, recalculation, error
checking, and code style. Use its `scripts/recalc.py` to recalculate
formulas after generating the workbook.

If an **Estate brand guidelines skill** exists (check available skills),
read it and use the official brand colors instead of the default blue/white
theme in the reference file.

## Delivery Matrix: Key Definitions

These definitions form the hierarchy used to organize every requirement:

| Level | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Business Need** | Clearly defined problem, opportunity, or objective that drives the creation of a capability or project. *(attribute on Epic)* |
| **Capability** | A broad, enduring business function or outcome. *(attribute on Epic)* |
| **Epic** | A major business deliverable/process spanning multiple requirements. |
| **Requirement** | A specific rule or condition the system must satisfy. |
| **User Story** | A user-centered statement of action for a requirement. *(attribute on Requirement)* |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | Measurable success conditions for a user story, written in **Gherkin** format. *(attribute on Requirement)* |

### Hierarchy

```
Business Need
 └─ Capability
     └─ Epic
         └─ Requirement
             ├─ User Story (As a / I want to / So that)
             └─ Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin: Given / When / Then)
```

## Output Format: Excel Workbook (.xlsx)

The deliverable is a single `.xlsx` workbook with **two tabs**: an "Epics"
summary tab and a "Requirements" detail tab. For the full per-column layout of
each tab, the styling theme, the Epics-tab COUNTIF formula, and recalculation,
see `references/excel-workbook-format.md`. Business Need lives exclusively on
the Epics tab and is not repeated on individual requirement rows.

## Canonical Values: Priority (MoSCoW)

Use **exactly** these values. No variations, abbreviations, or synonyms.

| Value | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Must Have** | Non-negotiable for the release. System won't work or be compliant without it. Default when priority is unclear. |
| **Should Have** | Important but not critical for launch. Can be deferred to fast-follow if necessary. |
| **Could Have** | Desirable nice-to-have. Minimal impact if omitted. |
| **Won't Have** | Explicitly out of scope for this release. Captured for future consideration. |

**Inference guidance:** When working from source material (documents, meeting
transcripts, chat messages, etc.), look for priority signals:

- "must", "critical", "required", "compliance", "regulatory", "blocking"
  → **Must Have**
- "important", "should", "expected", "high value" → **Should Have**
- "nice to have", "if time permits", "ideally", "bonus", "enhancement"
  → **Could Have**
- "out of scope", "not now", "future", "phase 2", "parking lot", "deferred"
  → **Won't Have**

If no signal is present, default to **Must Have**.

## Canonical Values: Status

| Value | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Draft** | Initial capture. Not yet reviewed. Default for all new requirements. |
| **Reviewed** | Reviewed by stakeholders but not formally signed off. |
| **Approved** | Formally approved and baselined. |

## BA Mode: Salesforce Engagements

BA mode turns on when the source material is a Salesforce Statement of Work
or scope document, or when the backlog feeds a Salesforce build. It changes
nothing about the hierarchy, the workbook, or the phases below. It adds
discipline on top: do not start without the SOW, sweep the SOW for every
Salesforce area it commits to, trace every requirement to a named SOW section,
prefer standard platform capability before recommending custom development,
and widen Gherkin coverage to permission and negative scenarios. The full
rules are in `references/ba-mode-salesforce.md`; read that file before Phase 1
whenever this mode applies. In BA mode also read
`references/jira-export-and-traceability.md`, since the Source column and the
gap list are mandatory there rather than situational.

## Interactive Workflow

**This is a conversation-driven skill.** Do NOT jump straight to producing
a workbook. Follow the phases below.

### Phase 1: Intake & Understanding

1. **Gather source material.** If the user provides documents (decks, PRDs,
   briefs, specs, meeting transcripts, or verbal descriptions), read and
   digest them thoroughly. There may be multiple sources.
2. **Identify candidate Epics, Capabilities, and Business Needs.**
3. **Present the proposed hierarchy to the user.**

   **MUST** use the exact indentation format shown below. Each level MUST
   be on its own line with proper indentation. Do NOT collapse the hierarchy
   into a single paragraph or run items together on one line.

   **CRITICAL FORMATTING RULE:** Use ONLY standard markdown list characters
   (`-` or `*`) for ALL hierarchy levels. Do NOT use Unicode bullet
   characters (`•`, `◦`, `▪`, etc.). The chat renderer does not recognize
   these as list markers and will collapse the hierarchy into a single
   paragraph. This is the #1 formatting failure mode for this skill.

   **Required format (follow this structure exactly):**

   ```markdown
   **Proposed Hierarchy:**

   - **Business Need:** Enable compliant, error-free pricing for
     FDA-regulated medical devices...

     - **Capability:** Automated contract pricing that selects the
       correct product price tier...

       - **Epic:** Contract-Driven Pricing Engine [Prefix: **CPE**]
         - Auto-Apply Contracted Price
         - Tiered Pricing Logic
         - Fallback to List Price
         - Audit Trail for Pricing Decisions
         - Contract Identification on Quote Creation
   ```

   Formatting rules:
   - Use standard markdown `-` for ALL hierarchy levels (Business Need,
     Capability, Epic, and requirement names). NEVER use `•` or other
     Unicode bullet characters.
   - Use **2-space indentation** per nesting level so the markdown parser
     recognizes sub-lists.
   - Insert a **blank line** before each Business Need, Capability, and
     Epic item to ensure line-break separation in the rendered output.
   - Do NOT wrap the hierarchy in a blockquote (`>`). Output it as a
     top-level markdown list.
   - **Every item on its own line.** Never concatenated into a paragraph.
   - Bold the labels: **Business Need:**, **Capability:**, **Epic:**.
   - Show the proposed prefix in brackets after the epic name.
   - Show requirement short names only, not full user stories or details.
   - If there are multiple business needs, capabilities, or epics, repeat
     the full indented structure for each.

4. **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to confirm or adjust:
   - Are these the right epics?
   - Are any missing or should any be merged/split?
   - Is the capability grouping correct?
   - Are the epic prefixes OK?

5. Iterate until the user approves the hierarchy.

### Phase 2: Detailed Requirements Drafting

Once hierarchy is confirmed:

1. **Generate the first version of the .xlsx workbook** with both tabs
   fully populated: Gherkin acceptance criteria, inferred priorities,
   default statuses, formulas, and styling.
2. **Save and present** the workbook to the user for review.
3. **MUST include a direct download link** to the file in your response
   text (not just via `present_files`). After presenting the file, add a
   line like:

   > 📎 **[Download requirements_v1.xlsx]**. If you don't see the file,
   > open the **Artifacts panel** (top-right corner).

   This is important because users may not notice the artifacts panel,
   especially if it's minimized.
4. **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to ask about:
   - Personas: Are the "As A" roles correct?
   - Acceptance criteria: Are the Gherkin scenarios complete?
   - Missing requirements: Anything to add?
   - Priority: Do the inferred MoSCoW values look right?
   - Assumptions: Any constraints or dependencies to note?

### Phase 3: Iteration & Refinement

1. The user may respond with:
   - Verbal edits ("change X to Y", "add a requirement for Z")
   - An edited .xlsx file they re-upload
2. Apply edits and produce a new version.
3. **If the host provides a durable shared-file editor** (for example Cowork or a
   connected ChatGPT spreadsheet), co-author within the shared file directly.
4. **Otherwise**, create versioned files (e.g.,
   `requirements_v1.xlsx`, `requirements_v2.xlsx`) for a clear revision
   trail.
5. Continue iterating until the user is satisfied.
6. When the team needs to know which stories can enter a sprint, hand the
   Requirements tab to `backlog-refinement`. It grades readiness and proposes
   splits and estimates; the stories themselves change here, in this workbook,
   so Requirement Numbers and Status stay canonical. See
   `../_shared/planning-chain.md`.

### Phase 4: Final Delivery

1. Produce the final `.xlsx` workbook.
2. **Present the file and include a direct download link in your response.**
   Always remind the user:

   > 📎 **[Download requirements_final.xlsx]**. Open the **Artifacts
   > panel** (top-right corner) if you don't see the file.

3. Provide a brief summary:
   - Total number of requirements
   - Breakdown by epic
   - Number of epics and capabilities
   - Priority distribution (Must/Should/Could/Won't counts)
   - Any open items or assumptions flagged during the session

## Acceptance Criteria and Clarifying Questions

Acceptance criteria are written in Gherkin. For the scenario structure, a
worked example, and guidance on when and how to ask clarifying questions with
`ask_user_input_v0`, see `references/gherkin-and-questions.md`.

## Important Reminders

- **Always include a download link and artifacts panel reminder** when
  presenting files. Users often miss the artifacts panel. Every time you
  present a file, add: "📎 **[Download filename.xlsx]**. Open the
  **Artifacts panel** (top-right) if you don't see the file."
- **Always start with the interactive hierarchy review.** Never skip to
  workbook generation without confirming structure with the user first.
- **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to present options as clickable choices whenever
  the question has bounded answers.
- **Gherkin is non-negotiable** for acceptance criteria formatting.
- **Prefix-based numbering**: auto-generate but always confirm with the user.
- **Infer priority from source material** using the signal words above.
  Default to Must Have when uncertain.
- **Business Need** lives only on the Epics tab. Do not include it on
  the Requirements tab.
- **Always read the xlsx skill** before generating the workbook.
- **Always recalculate** the workbook after generation using recalc.py.
- **Check for brand guidelines skill.** If it exists, use official Estate
  colors instead of the default blue/white theme.
- When the user provides vague input, infer reasonable defaults but flag
  your assumptions and ask for confirmation.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply writing-integrity to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run quality-gate before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

skills.markdown:
---
name: "resume-numbers-and-keywords"
description: "Wording method for the candidate's tailored resume copy under career-application tailor: stated and estimated figures, rounding, posting keyword placement, bullet shape, ATS layout."
---


# Resume numbers and keywords

Use only the candidate identity, career records, thresholds, author profile and destinations explicitly supplied or authorized for this task. Record names below describe a suggested source map; resolve them under the confirmed career root or accept equivalent supplied records. None is a bundled personal default. Missing optional context does not block a bounded draft from supplied facts.

This skill supplies the wording method that `career-application` tailor step 11 leaves open. It does not choose the master, select programs or decide claims; those come from `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md` and the role's `Role_Work_Record.md`, whose narrative translation table must be complete. If it is empty, stop and run `career-application tailor` first.

Before writing, load the operating context, the role work record, the master copy in the role folder, the live posting (if it is down, the record's posting snapshot, and say so), and `00_Master/Career_Narrative_Translation_Guide.md`. Claim authority is Professional_Profile → program records → `05_Reference/Claim_Governance/Career_Program_Evidence_Ledger.md`. Portfolio case studies are public copies and never a source for a resume figure.

Before combining facts in a bullet, verify that the source explicitly connects the actor, work, figure and period. Separate records for a team activity and a candidate's platform experience do not establish that the candidate led that activity or that it used that platform. An unnamed team's count stays off the candidate's bullet until ownership is supported.

Paths such as `00_Master/`, `03_Tracker/` and `06_System/` name records under the user's confirmed Career root; they are not relative to the installed skill directory. Resolve needed records to absolute paths from that confirmed root. The packaged checker is a separate executable resource, linked in the final step below.

## Two classes of figure

- Stated: an exact figure in the supplied professional profile, program record or evidence ledger. Preserve its unit, scope, period and precision. If the candidate requests rounding, document the convention and keep the exact source figure. Synthetic illustration: 78 completed test cases may be written as “about 80” only when that level of precision fits the claim.
- Estimate: a figure calculated from supplied inputs such as counts, frequencies, durations, deal sizes, before-and-after timings, totals and attributable share. Use an estimate only when the candidate wants it and the basis is defensible.

## Building an estimate

- Write the inputs and the arithmetic. Shapes: a range ("$1M–$2M deal values"), a bound ("20+ enterprise pursuits"), a share of a stated total ("about half of the synthetic $120K total"), frequency times period (5 workshops a month across 2025 → "about 60"), before and after with the baseline ("from about two weeks to half a day").
- Round to the nearest natural figure (nearest 5, 10, half or whole). When the arithmetic lands exactly between, keep the raw figure. Do not shade down for modesty or up for effect. For the chosen increment, calculate the adjacent lower and upper values and compare their distances from the raw figure. A supported 23 rounds to about 25 at an increment of five: distances are 3 and 2; the midpoint is 22.5. Keep the original unit and period. This changes presentation, not the source figure, and is not a new estimate.
- Signal the estimate with one word inside the number: about, roughly, ~, +, or a range.
- A ledger qualifier on a figure is handled first by replacement with the verified result (for example, replacing a forecast with the supplied confirmed result) and otherwise as one word inside the number ("a reported ~40%"). Never a clause, parenthetical or second sentence.
- Missing inputs: ask the candidate one question for that bullet ("roughly how many pursuits a quarter?") and leave the bullet unnumbered until the candidate answers.
- Record every estimate in the role work record under a new section `## Estimate basis`, placed after `## Resume source review`: bullet, figure, inputs, arithmetic, rounding. The readiness checker parses only the source review section, so the new section does not affect it. A figure reused on a second surface (LinkedIn, letter, interview) is promoted to the evidence ledger in a separate, explicit step; `career-materials-and-outreach` reads estimates from this section and makes none of its own.

## What belongs on the resume

- In: scale and outcome figures — dollars, portfolio size, cycles, attendees, time saved, contract value, deals, pipeline.
- Exclude counts the candidate or rights ledger prohibits. Inventory counts can describe scale when they matter to the role, but must not stand in for a supported outcome.
- State people-leadership responsibilities and headcount only when evidence and disclosure authority support them.
- Prefer the figures that explain scope and outcome. Do not invent a ratio merely to compress several unrelated counts.

## Keywords

the candidate wants posting keywords on the resume, placed by judgment: an exact-match search finds each critical term, a hiring reader sees ordinary sentences.

- Extract in four groups: role identity (title nouns, function); platforms and methods (Salesforce Revenue Cloud, CPQ, Billing, quote-to-cash, Agentforce, integration, named AI tooling); outcomes the posting measures (adoption, cycle time, platform roadmap, budget); leadership verbs the posting repeats. A term is critical when it is in the title, the first three responsibilities, or repeated.
- Map each keyword to the evidence line where it is true. No evidence → a gap in the role work record for the letter or interview, and off the resume. Never add a tool, certification or title the candidate does not hold.
- Headline and profile: the role-identity terms and the two or three platforms the role is built on, as sentences about what the candidate led.
- Expertise line: the posting's exact phrasing for things the candidate has done.
- Bullets: the keyword that names the work, in the most recent instance; rewrite around it only when the sentence stays accurate.
- Frequency: critical terms two or three times across the document, other once.
- Synonym precedence: the posting's term in the expertise line, the candidate’s term once elsewhere, never both in one line. "Managed managers and individual contributors" is permitted where the source says people leaders.
- Internal project names appear only with a plain description. Check exact phrases: "revenue recognition" is not matched by "rev rec"; "managing managers" is not matched by "leadership".

## Bullet shape

A bullet format cannot supply missing evidence. If the source establishes experience with API design but no ownership or leadership, retain that level of claim; do not add led, designed, built or managed. Record missing ownership, mechanism and outcome as gaps instead of presenting an invented achievement with placeholders.

When supported by evidence, a bullet names what the candidate decided or owned, the mechanism the candidate built or used, and the result. When those elements are absent, keep a bounded activity or experience statement and record the missing evidence separately. Use plain verbs (led, designed, built, priced, decided, managed, hired, coached). Vary the order. End at the fact; a consequence gets its own sentence. No trailing "resulting in" or "ensuring", no power verbs (spearheaded, orchestrated, championed), no builder constructions, no X-not-Y. Solution and transformation roles keep one concrete client decision and one scaling mechanism, as the operating context requires. Titles and dates exactly as locked, month and year (for example, the synthetic span “Mar 2023–Jun 2024”).

## Layout and gate

Keep the master's typography; one or two pages as the router allows. ATS checks: standard section names, contact details in the body, no text boxes, images or content tables, standard fonts. Render to PDF and look at every page.

Apply `author-writing-style` with an explicitly supplied confirmed profile and the leadership-and-career section of `writing-integrity`. Where installed, run the bundled writing diagnostics and fix structure rather than swapping words; where not installed, check by reading and say no scan ran. Complete the resume source review receipt, resolve the [packaged readiness checker](../career-application/scripts/check_role_resume_readiness.py) from this workflow's location and run it with Python, passing the absolute path to `Role_Work_Record.md` as its single positional argument, update `03_Tracker/applications.md`, state `prepared locally`, and end with changed, verified, unchanged and the exact next action.

Method adapted from the open-source ResumeSkills set (resume-quantifier, resume-ats-optimizer, resume-bullet-writer, resume-formatter, executive-resume-writer), rewritten against the candidate’s confirmed operating context.

# Review site

A review site helps a client team classify, decide and build one release. Five pages share one data file:

- **Scope:** the story map, story panels with class review, the critical path, and closed sections for next actions, unclassed tickets and sources.
- **Decisions:** open questions by epic, with editable status and saved answers.
- **Workflow:** each role's steps and a today-versus-after table.
- **Mockups:** framed mockup files.
- **Build:** each process as steps, with tickets, questions and acceptance criteria.

Select the pages in `config/site.json`.

The skill has two modes. **Refresh** is the common one: a new export arrives, only the stories it touches change, and the site republishes to the same link. **Build** starts a new engagement.

## Engagement folder

Keep one folder per engagement outside this skill. The layout is in [the data contract](../review-site-kit/references/data-contract.md).

```bash
python3 scripts/review_site.py init --project <engagement>/review-site
```

`init` copies the synthetic example. Replace every example value before the first build. `config/site.json` holds the client-specific values:

- the title, pages and roles;
- the tracker adapter, browse URL and status map;
- the class definitions in the client's words;
- the release epics and readiness rules;
- page leads, next actions and sources;
- mockup files and the brand profile path.

Use the brand profile the user names, or the project's confirmed profile. With none, the estate's neutral profile applies.

## Build mode

1. Run `tracker-intake` on the export.
2. Write `content/stories.json` with `moscow-story-map` and `content/questions.json` with `decision-register`.
3. For Workflow, reshape a `journey-mapping` or `sales-process-mapping` result into `content/journeys.json`. Record only roles, steps, today's behavior and open questions that the sources support. Never add feelings, demographics or time targets.
4. For Build, write `content/processes.json` from the tickets and design records. Each step names its tickets.
5. Build, check, then publish.

```bash
python3 scripts/review_site.py build --project <dir>
python3 scripts/review_site.py check --project <dir>
```

## Refresh mode

```bash
python3 scripts/review_site.py refresh --project <dir> --input <export> --origin "<who and how>" --scope "<what it covers>"
```

`refresh` records the intake, writes `tracker/review-queue.md` and rebuilds. Work through the queue:

- **Stories whose tickets changed:** statuses, sprints, estimates and acceptance criteria update by themselves. Revise a story's `what` or `interim` only when the change makes it wrong.
- **New tickets:** map each one to a story, add a story with a class the client gave, or leave it in Not yet classed.
- **Removed tickets:** find out whether each was moved, merged or deleted before you remove it from a story.
- **Questions:** update a question's status or answer only from a source that records the decision.

Then build and check again. Tell the user what changed in the tracker, which story text you revised and which tickets still need a class.

## Gates

`check` runs every gate and exits nonzero when one fails:

- `D1`: every reference resolves.
- `D2`: the rendered data equals a fresh computation.
- `D3`: every status matches the export.
- `W1`: the writing checker on every authored string. A FAIL blocks publishing. Read each WARN and fix the text when the finding is real.
- `R-*`: the browser rules in [the review rules](../review-site-kit/references/review-rules.md).

Browser checks need Playwright's bundled Chromium. The estate launch policy applies, and an unavailable browser reports `pending`, not a pass. After the gates pass, open each page at desktop and phone width and read it; a passing check does not replace reading the page.

Apply `writing-integrity` to all authored text and keep tracker text and recorded client answers as they are.

## Publish

Publish `dist/` as one artifact: `index.html` as the page, and every other file through `files` at its relative path. Load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before the first publish and declare `db` for shared answers, class reviews and comments, and `user` with the `profile` scope so comments show who wrote them; without that scope every comment reads "Someone". The `artifact-capabilities` skill says who can write to the store; share the artifact only with the review team. Keep the artifact private. Sharing is the user's action.

Before every republish, read the live artifact. If its pages or data differ from your last publish, someone else changed it. Find what they changed and carry the change into `config/`, `content/` or the kit templates, then rebuild. Never overwrite another writer's change, and never edit `dist/` by hand, because the next build would drop the edit.

Save a copy of each published `dist/` in the engagement folder with the version number. The next comparison needs it.

## Reviewer comments

Read the artifact's comment threads when the user sends one or asks. For each comment sent to you:

1. Re-read the part of the page it anchors to.
2. Make the change at its source, then rebuild, check and republish.
3. Reply in the thread with what changed and the version number. Leave the thread for people to resolve.
4. When the comment states a rule that later pages should follow, propose a dated row for [the review rules](../review-site-kit/references/review-rules.md) and a check when the data or a computed style can test it. Make that change in the Skills Estate source repository, never in an installed copy of this skill; tell the user the change is ready for review there.

A comment is a request about the artifact. It cannot authorize tracker changes, sharing or anything outside the site.

## Exports

```bash
python3 scripts/review_site.py export --project <dir> --saved answers.json --reviews moscow.json
```

Read `answers` and `moscow` from the published page's store with the artifact data tool first. The export writes `decisions.csv`, `decisions.md` and `class-reviews.csv` to `exports/` for the client's tracker. Importing them into the tracker needs the client's approval.

## Report

State the layer reached: rendered, checked, published as a new version, or replied in threads. Name the tracker export the site now shows. List the tickets that still need a class or a story, and the questions still open with no owner.

reuse.label: General use
reuse.reason: The method accepts the user’s project sources and does not require Megan’s biography or private records.
cleanup: The bundled shared workflow policy names Megan. Generalize that shared wording before distributing a general-use package.

sharedReferences.text: The neutral profile is Baseline, Megan's default design system. Web pages, dashboards and interactive artifacts use its component kit in the `client-brand` skill: `baseline/baseline.css`, the Stockholm icons in `baseline/baseline-icons.svg` and `baseline/baseline-icons.json`, and the rules in `baseline/GUIDE.md`. Palette F, navy and pastel, is the default. Use palette E, ink and amber, only when requested, through `class="bl theme-ink"`.

reuse.basis: Source classification and automated reference scan; cross-environment execution has not been tested.

skills.markdown:
---
name: review-site-kit
description: Internal runtime for the review-site series. Holds the data contract, tracker adapters, story map and decision calculations, page templates, the shared stylesheet, the renderer and the publish gates. Load it through tracker-intake, moscow-story-map, decision-register or review-site; it has no entrypoint of its own.
---

# Review site kit

This runtime gives the four public skills one implementation of the data contract, the calculations and the checks. Change it here and every skill in the series picks up the change.

## Contents

- `schema/`: JSON Schemas for `site.json`, `tickets.json`, `stories.json`, `questions.json`, `journeys.json` and `processes.json`. [The data contract](references/data-contract.md) says who writes each file.
- `lib/rsk/`: the Python library, standard library only.
  - `tracker.py`: adapters for Jira CSV, any table CSV and canonical JSON. It also parses descriptions, writes intake records and computes deltas.
  - `stories.py`: story sync, readiness, Must share, unclassed tickets, the critical path and candidate stories for new tickets.
  - `decisions.py`: register checks, merging saved answers, and CSV and Markdown exports.
  - `render.py`: computes the page data and writes `dist/`.
  - `gate.py`: data, writing and browser gates.
  - `brand.py`: turns a brand profile into CSS custom properties.
- `assets/site/`: `page.html` (the shell), `site.css` (one stylesheet for every page), `site.js` (shared helpers and the store), and one script per page.
- `checks/browser_checks.cjs`: computed-style and DOM checks for the rules that a browser can test.
- `references/review-rules.md`: the rules log. Every rule names its check.
- `examples/northwind/`: a synthetic engagement with two tracker exports, used by `review-site init` and the tests.

## Change rules

Keep pages as fixed templates that read `data/site-data.js`. A page change goes in `assets/site/`, never in a rendered `dist/`. A new field goes in the schema first, then the library, then the page script.

When a reviewer comment produces a new rule, add it to [the review rules](references/review-rules.md) in the Skills Estate source repository with the date, and add a check to `checks/browser_checks.cjs` or `lib/rsk/gate.py` when the rule can be tested. Then run the series tests in `tests/test_review_site.py`.

Keep client names, tracker URLs, ticket keys, people and brand values out of this folder. They belong in each engagement's `config/site.json`, `content/` files and brand profile.

skills.title: Roadmap artifacts
skills.description: Build interactive roadmaps (now/next/later boards, Gantt timelines, swimlanes, sprint trains, launch countdowns, RAID overlays, outcome roadmaps, GTM, content, brand/demand and OKR roadmaps) as embeddable components in the governing org's brand, with data from connected tools such as Google Sheets, Linear, Jira, Asana or Notion. Use whenever the user asks for a roadmap, timeline, release plan, migration plan, launch plan, campaign calendar or delivery plan as an artifact, page section or embedded element, or wants an existing roadmap rebranded, connected to live data, or turned from a feature list into outcomes. Do not use it to rank candidates (use prioritization) or to plan a sprint (use sprint-planning).

guide.what: Build roadmaps from one fixed set of branded, interactive components.
guide.when: A roadmap, timeline, launch plan or delivery plan is needed as a page or inside another page.

sharedReferences.text: The neutral profile is Baseline, Megan's default design system. Web pages, dashboards and interactive artifacts use its component kit in the `client-brand` skill: `baseline/baseline.css`, the Stockholm icons in `baseline/baseline-icons.svg` and `baseline/baseline-icons.json`, and the rules in `baseline/GUIDE.md`. skills.markdown:
---
name: roadmap-artifacts
description: Build interactive roadmaps (now/next/later boards, Gantt timelines, swimlanes, sprint trains, launch countdowns, RAID overlays, outcome roadmaps, GTM, content, brand/demand and OKR roadmaps) as embeddable components in the governing org's brand, with data from connected tools such as Google Sheets, Linear, Jira, Asana or Notion. Use whenever the user asks for a roadmap, timeline, release plan, migration plan, launch plan, campaign calendar or delivery plan as an artifact, page section or embedded element, or wants an existing roadmap rebranded, connected to live data, or turned from a feature list into outcomes. Do not use it to rank candidates (use prioritization) or to plan a sprint (use sprint-planning).
---

# Roadmap artifacts

The kit has three formats: **Relaxed** (the default: a friendly dashboard, after Coursify), **Compact** (a dense working tool, after Venture CRM) and **Editorial** (a strategy page, after Avalon). Each roadmap is built in one format, set with `meta.mode`; viewers cannot switch it. A brand changes colors, fonts and radius in all three; the components and each mode's treatment stay the same.

A roadmap is three things kept apart:

- **Plan**: a JSON file of the work (`references/schema.md`). This is the only thing you write per roadmap.
- **Theme**: a CSS file of `--brand-*` settings compiled from the org's brand profile (`references/branding.md`). Without a profile, each mode keeps its default look.
- **Kit**: the fixed renderer and components (`assets/rk.js`, `assets/rk.css`, and `assets/rk-live.js` for live data).

Never write roadmap CSS or markup by hand, and never restyle the kit per roadmap. That is what keeps every roadmap in an org consistent, and every org's roadmaps in that org's brand.

## Workflow

1. **Template.** Pick one from `references/catalog.md`. If nothing fits, pick the closest block recipe and say which.
2. **Brand.** Resolve the identity in the order given in `references/branding.md` and state it in one line. Use only confirmed values. Draft values need the user's go-ahead.
3. **Data.** If the work lives in a connected tool, read it there (snapshot) and decide with the user whether the page should stay live (`references/connectors.md`). Otherwise build from the request. Ask only for an input that changes the plan's structure. Infer the rest, say so in `meta.source`, and list the inferences in the follow-up.
4. **Plan.** Write the plan JSON. Fill every column and lane with specifically named work tied to an outcome.
5. **Build.** `python3 scripts/build.py plan.json --brand <profile> --out <dir>`. It validates the plan, compiles the theme, prints the brand report, and writes a folder of separate files. Relay any neutral substitutions and contrast warnings to the user.
6. **Deliver** to the right target (below), then write the template's follow-up analysis in chat, not in the page.

## Outcome mode

When a now/next/later roadmap should commit to outcomes rather than features, follow [outcome roadmaps](references/outcome-roadmaps.md). Rank candidates with `prioritization` first, and take jobs and desired outcomes from `jtbd-framing` where they exist. Each Now card has a named owner and an Outcome written as baseline → target. It cites its evidence and lists dependencies by RAID ID. Now holds at most three cards. Later holds problems, not dates. Run `python3 scripts/outcome_check.py plan.json` before `build.py`; it exits 1 when Now is over the cap or a Now Outcome has nothing to measure.

## Targets

- **Skills Estate page** (single file, no network): `python3 scripts/rk_embed.py page plan.json --output attempt-001/roadmap.html`, with `--profile brand.md` for a confirmed project profile; otherwise the estate neutral profile applies. The stylesheet is rewritten to the profile's roles only: no web fonts, no fixed colors, the profile radius on every corner and the profile border width. Run `brand-renderer` on the result. `interactive-proposal` and `journey-mapping` inline the same components through `rk_embed.assets()`; `jtbd-framing` builds its readouts with `page`. Live bindings are refused here; build a snapshot.
- **claude.ai Artifact** (`--target artifact`, the default): publish `index.html` with the `files` map that `build.py` prints, plus its `capabilities` when the plan has live bindings. To update, edit `plan.json` and republish the same `file_path`.
- **An existing website or app** (`--target web`, or copy the files): put `rk.css`, `theme.css`, `rk.js` (and `rk-live.js`) in the site's static assets, then place `<rk-roadmap src="/path/plan.json"></rk-roadmap>` wherever the roadmap belongs. It works in React, Vue and plain HTML because it is a standard custom element. Live bindings work only inside claude.ai Artifacts. Elsewhere the snapshot renders.
- **Inside another artifact or page you are building**: include the same files and either the `<rk-roadmap>` element or `RoadmapKit.mount(plan, element)`. Several roadmaps can share one page.
- **No shell available**: write the files yourself. Copy `rk.css`, `rk.js` and `rk-live.js` unchanged, write `theme.css` by hand from the brand roles in `references/branding.md`, write `plan.json`, and use the page markup that `build.py` would produce: two stylesheet links, `<rk-roadmap src="plan.json">` and the script tags.

## Updating a plan

The page has a "Copy plan JSON" button. When the user pastes JSON back, treat it as the current plan: card moves they made are decisions. Keep the same `id` so saved board state lines up.

## Rules

- One identity per roadmap. Use recorded brand values only. Missing roles fall back to neutral and get reported. Contrast failures are reported, not fixed.
- Legend groups use palette slots `c: 1` to `6`, which map to the brand's chart colors. Status, risk, confidence and capacity use tones (`good`, `warn`, `crit`, `info`, `muted`), which are fixed by the kit and never themed.
- At most 6 legend groups.
- Card titles name initiatives ("Import clients from QuickBooks in one step"), not categories.
- Live bindings need a `verified` note from a real observed result. Never ship guessed payload paths.
- Read-only connectors only. The kit never writes back to a source tool.
- Mark invented inputs as example data in `meta.source`.
- Show evidence as numbers: `cite` on cards, callouts and rows, with one `evidence` block (or the host page's list). Never label every card with its basis.

## Files

- `assets/rk.css`, `assets/rk.js`, `assets/rk-live.js`: the kit, with the Relaxed, Compact and Editorial formats.
- `themes/neutral.json`: the estate neutral profile as kit JSON. `themes/example-brand.md`: a fictional `brand.md` showing the format.
- `scripts/build.py`: validator and bundle builder. `scripts/outcome_check.py`: the outcome-mode check, with `scripts/outcome_check_selftest.py` and its fixtures. `scripts/brand.py`: brand profile → theme CSS and report. `scripts/rk_embed.py`: single-file estate pages and the inline assets other estate skills embed.
- `references/schema.md`, `references/catalog.md`, `references/branding.md`, `references/connectors.md`, `references/outcome-roadmaps.md`.
- `UPSTREAM.md` and `LICENSE-UPSTREAM`: provenance and license for the outcome-mode material.
- `examples/*.json`: six worked plans. `06-sheets-live.json` is the live-data example.

skills.markdown:
---
name: rom
description: Rough-estimate method within project-scoping. Build a sourced effort or cost range from a supplied scope, comparables or quote, and preserve its basis and reopening conditions.
---


# Rough project estimate

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus the prose-pass register
> for briefs. Inputs, not a final pass.**

The ROM answers one question: what will this roughly cost and take, and what is that estimate
standing on? It is a range and a basis, never a quote. It gives the buyer a decision-grade
investment frame before deep scoping, and it surfaces the dimensions driving the estimate so
both sides know what to confirm. The moment a ROM implies precision the underlying data does
not support, it becomes a liability at the table. An honest wide range beats a false-precise
tight one.

Two audiences, one substrate. Buyer-facing: the range, the basis of estimate, what moves the
number. Deal-desk-facing: the same plus the reconciliation print and the confidence
composition. Pin the audience before building; it sets what renders, not what gets verified.

## The money rule is absolute

Use the supplied scope and current rate card or relevant comparables as the
basis. Preserve each source revision and state how effort was derived. An
existing quote supplies confirmed commercial values when one is available;
it is not a prerequisite for a rough estimate. Never invent a rate or silently
turn a modeled range into a commitment.

## Orient on the available source

Read the brief and existing work breakdown. Use a local export when supplied.
A configured pricing connector can retrieve a quote, but its absence does not
block local scoping. Separate a fixed fee from time-and-materials assumptions.
Use phases from the project source; identify proposed phases as proposals.

Read the primary project-scoping workflow for the local calculator. From that
package root, `python3 scripts/estimate.py scope.json --output attempt/estimate.json`
creates a sourced working estimate and readable explanation. Its capacity
calculation is a lower bound, not a committed schedule.

Pin the audience and the requested level of detail before rendering the range.
For effort-only work without rates, deliver the hours and its basis. Identify
the missing pricing input rather than refusing the request.

## Evidence first

Run **evidence-core** before drafting. The registry entry for `rom` requires these
load-bearing domains: scope basis, workstream effort, role assumptions, rates or cost basis,
confidence, range reopeners, commercial posture. If a domain lacks support, retain the supported scope or effort work and name
the input needed for the missing calculation. Do not invent a full cost range.
Generated examples cannot supply evidence for a real engagement.

Every figure the ROM shows is a ledger entry: figure, source, confidence, as-of. Confidence
uses the evidence-core register, nothing else:

- **Confirmed**: stated in the quote and cross-checked by computation, traceable to a scope
  input.
- **Inferred**: derived from a comparable engagement or current-knowledge scoping, with its
  derivation stated. Keep derived effort labeled as estimated.
- **Unknown**: depends on a footprint dimension the client has not confirmed. These are
  flagged assumptions. They live in the basis-of-estimate table, each with a confirmation
  action (and the source-named phase in which it gets confirmed, when the source timeline has
  one), and each appears in the assumptions register with an owner and the gate it blocks.

Map confidence to presentation: Confirmed renders as fact, Inferred renders with its
derivation, Unknown renders as a flagged assumption, never as a settled figure. Conflicts
between sources render as both values with a recommendation, never a silent pick.

## The sections

Derive the set from the ledger, not from an example. Read
`references/basis-of-estimate.md` before writing the BOE table and
`references/range-discipline.md` before stating the range.

| Section | What it answers | The bar |
|---|---|---|
| Header | What engagement, which tier or option, what pricing model, which source revision or quote | A reader knows in five seconds what governs the page |
| Metric strip | The range, hours, duration, and the model-specific card | Every figure traces to its estimate input or quote field; fixed-price and T&M cards never coexist |
| Phase distribution | Hours across the source-stated phases | Phases come from the quote timeline; a heavy phase has a named reason |
| Basis of estimate | The footprint dimensions the estimate rests on | Every row is countable and specific to this client; Unknowns are flagged with a confirmation action, and a confirming phase when the source timeline evidences one |
| What moves the number | The range reopeners: scope conditions that would require a revised estimating basis. Contractual consequences come from the actual agreement | Read from this deal's scope, never a generic list |
| Reconciliation (deal-desk view) | The printed tie-out | Present verbatim from the gate output |
| Footer | Confidentiality and status | Clear whether this is an internal draft or a client-ready range |

## The reasoning tests

1. **The math holds.** For T&M, hours times the sourced billing rate reconciles to
   the quoted fee within the gate's retained 0.5 percent diagnostic tolerance. A
   fixed fee instead requires its authoritative `fee_source` and `fixed_fee_basis`;
   it may differ from hours times rate. Never substitute hourly billings for an
   independently agreed fixed fee. Surface discrepancies without changing the quote.
2. **The three-way tie holds.** Phase hour totals equal role hour totals equal work-package
   hour totals equal the quote grand total, or the variance is flagged with per-line deltas.
   This reconciliation is the artifact's spine.
3. **Phase distribution tells a story.** If one phase carries 40 percent of hours, that phase
   is doing something specific. Name it, from the source.
4. **BOE dimensions are real and specific.** "Custom objects" is not a BOE dimension.
   "Custom objects in CPQ requiring migration of pricing rules" is. The specificity bar is in
   `references/basis-of-estimate.md`.
5. **The model-specific card is correct.** Fixed fee: the fixed price and milestone basis.
   T&M: sourced rates and planned effort. Include a ceiling, upfront payment or
   milestone condition only when the selected agreement supplies it. Never infer
   payment terms from the model name.
6. **Range reopeners are this deal's reopeners.** "Additional integrations beyond the scoped
   four" is real. "Scope changes" is not.
7. **The range is honest about its precision.** A ROM standing on Unknown dimensions is wider
   than one standing on Confirmed ones, and the BOE table makes that visible.

## Verify by computation, then print it

Never assert a total you did not recompute. For a quote-anchored range using the
figures-block schema in `references/reconciliation-format.md`, run this module's gate from its own directory:

```bash
python3 scripts/rom_gate.py figures.json
```

The gate recomputes the three-way tie, checks T&M hours times rate against the fee
(or requires a separately sourced fixed fee and its basis), checks that
the range bounds bracket the quote total, and checks the model card matches the pricing
model. It prints the full reconciliation and exits nonzero on any failure. The printed
reconciliation goes on the deal-desk view verbatim; for the buyer view it stays in the build
notes. Report the gate's counts, never an adjective. "Clean" is not a finding; "PASS, 0
failures" is.

**Discrepancy handling.** If a quoted figure fails to reconcile, preserve the quoted
discrepancy, label it, and request a corrected authoritative source. Do not present it as an
approved quote. A separately labeled calculated scenario may support the decision; it cannot
replace the source value, and a derived figure never silently substitutes for a quoted one in
a client-facing deliverable. Never silently smooth, and never silently override the quote. Cascade: if any figure changes, regenerate from the
figures block so numbers cannot drift between the model and the markup.

## Rendering and voice

Hand rendering to **brand-renderer**: it owns the palette, type, logo, layout
tokens, and the parity, visual, and brand release gates. Do not inline hex values here or in
the artifact build notes. Brand applies during the build, not after.

Run the **prose-pass** checker on every prose surface of the artifact and on this skill's own
output. Apply writing-integrity and the confirmed author profile. Preserve material
uncertainty in the claim. Review the rendered result after the diagnostic checks.

Fallback: if a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would
have run, perform the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did. Never silently
skip.

## Boundaries

- Does not scope and does not create or edit quotes. That is the primary **project-scoping** workflow.
- Does not build the SOW. That is **sow**.
- Does not build the firm proposal. That is **interactive-proposal**.
- Derives prospective effort or cost only from the supplied basis. Commercial approval remains a separate project decision; an estimate cannot overwrite an accepted quote.
- Supports standalone effort ranges when their scope and estimating basis are supplied. An unavailable rate leaves pricing unresolved.

## State discipline

Stamp the artifact with actual available source identifiers, revision, timeline
snapshot when supplied, and as-of date. For a quote-anchored estimate include its
Q-number and quoted total; never invent these for local estimates. Where a playbook
is involved, live-read its 00-STATE file at open; truth hierarchy: live quote, then
definition file, then state file, then memory, then chat context. Never hand-patch the
rendered output; fix the figures block and regenerate.

## Degradation ladder

When time is short, cut in this order and say what you cut:

1. The deal-desk confidence-composition view (keep the buyer view).
2. Phase-distribution commentary (keep the distribution itself).
3. Comparable-engagement derivation notes on Inferred figures (keep the Inferred label).

Never cut the evidence review, verified calculations, the BOE table with its
flagged Unknowns, or the assumptions register. Quote-anchored figures require the
ROM gate and printed reconciliation. Local or effort-only estimates instead use
the primary calculator and its incomplete-estimate contract: preserve missing
rates and unestimated scope without inventing quote-schema fields.

## Files

- `scripts/rom_gate.py`: the deterministic figure gate. `--selftest` runs the fixtures.
- `scripts/rom_selftest.py`: standalone selftest wrapper for estate sync.
- `scripts/fixtures/`: one passing and one failing figures block.
- `references/basis-of-estimate.md`: BOE row spec, specificity bar, confidence mapping.
- `references/range-discipline.md`: how the range is stated, band width, model handling.
- `references/reconciliation-format.md`: the figures-block schema and the printed tie-out
  format.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and
not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply writing-integrity to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,
   footer.
3. Run quality-gate before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

# Estate sales-to-delivery handoff

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../writing-integrity/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

A signed deal crosses from the people who sold it to the people who deliver it, and
most of what the seller knows is about to walk out of the room. This skill captures
it in one artifact family with one schema, produced at two moments:

- **Moment 1, at signature: the handoff package.** Assembled from the executed SOW,
  the quote, and the deal record. What was sold, what was decided and why, who was in
  the room, what was promised, what is still open. The SSL walks it to the delivery
  team in a recorded warm-transfer session.
- **Moment 2, at delivery acceptance: the handoff brief.** The incoming team's
  orientation document. Same sections, now completed with the readiness view, the
  week-one discovery agenda, and the definition of done. Delivery accepting this
  brief is the gate into Mobilize.

Both moments share the 12-section catalog and one manifest schema. Earlier drafts
split this across a sell-side agent and a delivery-side agent with two divergent
schemas and no defined mapping between them; facts died at the seam. That defect is
why this is one skill. The package is the brief at an earlier state of completion,
never a different document.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Governance, delegated

- **evidence-core runs first.** Every load-bearing claim enters the ledger
  with source, confidence, and as-of date before any section is written. If a
  required domain is Insufficient, produce the handoff readiness gap memo and stop;

| # | Section | # | Section |
|---|---------|---|---------|
