# sf-deploy-engine — operating the pipeline

The engine is an always-on orchestrator that owns Salesforce deployments to
**pipeline environments** through GitHub webhooks, one single-threaded FSM worker
per environment, and strict git-to-org synchronization. It takes over at the
first environment branch and owns everything upward.

**This skill starts at the PR into an environment branch.** Everything before
that — the ticket, the worktree, the local dry run, the deploy to your own dev
sandbox, the git and agent lifecycle hooks that enforce it — is `sf-delivery-standards`,
and that skill works the same whether or not an engine sits above it. Do not
duplicate its rules here and do not answer local-loop questions from this skill.

**This is a layer, not a fork.** The engine ships its own two guards
(`scripts/init.sh` installs them), which read `pipeline.yml` and nothing else.
They add refusals on top of the local-loop stack, read none of its config, and
write none of its files. **An agent working the local loop needs to know nothing
about this layer and change nothing to accommodate it.** If you find yourself
about to edit `sf-delivery-standards` to make something here work, stop — that
is the seam being crossed, and the answer is a rule in this skill's own hooks.

**What the guards bind, stated precisely.** A Claude or Codex hook fires on a tool
call the *model* makes. A command a human types in a terminal or runs from an IDE
never passes through the harness. So the true claim is *"an agent cannot deploy
to a pipeline org through this session"* — **not** *"the pipeline orgs are
protected."* The controls that bind a human are branch protection and the org's
own permissions. Do not let anyone read more into a green `doctor.sh` than that.

---

## Sub-commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/sf-deploy-engine` (no args) | Operate the pipeline. The default: status, promote, release, rollback, retry, revalidate. |
| `/sf-deploy-engine doctor` | Is this pipeline actually healthy? Read-only. `scripts/doctor.sh` |
| `/sf-deploy-engine init` | Point an existing repo at an already-running engine. `scripts/init.sh` |
| `/sf-deploy-engine provision` | Stand up a **new** engine instance: GCP, GitHub App, secrets, SSO. [references/provisioning.md](references/provisioning.md) |

Route on the argument: *status / promote / release / rollback / retry / frozen /
revalidate / what needs to ship* → operate. *doctor / audit / health / is the
engine ok / drift* → doctor. *init / onboard this repo / point at the engine* →
init. *provision / new instance / new client / GCP / GitHub App / rotate keys /
add an environment / build the vsix* → provisioning.

Provisioning is rare and one-time-per-client. It lives in a reference so it never
loads during a deploy.

---

## The boundary — get this right before anything else

| Where | Who deploys | How |
|---|---|---|
| Your dev sandbox | **You**, directly | `sf project deploy start`, governed by `sf-delivery-standards` |
| Any environment in `pipeline.yml` | **The engine**, exclusively | PR → engine validates → merge → engine deploys |

**Never run `sf project deploy` against a pipeline environment's org, for any
reason, including to fix something.** A manual deploy desyncs `deployed/<branch>`
from the org and the engine has no way to detect it. The recovery is Pause →
reconcile git and the tag by hand → Resume, and it is worse than whatever you
were trying to shortcut.

The two exceptions the schema allows are both narrow. `tier: sandbox` rows are
registered for **visibility only** — they produce the Dev Sandboxes board column
and are a legal `/api/release` source into a route entry point, but get no
worker, no `deployed/<branch>` tag and no engine-driven deploy. And `freeze:
advisory` relaxes the freeze gate for low-stakes tiers. Neither makes a sandbox
engine-managed. See `docs/decisions/sandboxes-are-environments.md` in the engine
repo before proposing otherwise.

---

## Core model

| Ref | Means | Moved by |
|---|---|---|
| Branch HEAD (`preprod`) | **Desired** org state | Merged PRs |
| Tag `deployed/<branch>` | **Actual** org state | The engine only |

Deltas are computed `deployed/<branch>` → SHA with sfdx-git-delta. A failed
deploy leaves the tag unmoved, so git still describes the org *at the tag* and
the gap stays queryable.

```
SETTLED → DEPLOYING → SETTLED (tag advanced)
             ↓ failure
          FROZEN → retry → DEPLOYING
             ↓ rollback (the revert lands as a push)
          DEPLOYING → SETTLED
```

Quick deploy (skip the 15-minute test run on merge) is eligible only when all
three hold: the validation ran on the same SHA, the org state is unchanged (the
tag has not moved), and the validation is under 10 days old. Any miss falls back
to a full deploy — that fallback is the design, not a bug.

**Fail-closed by construction:** engine down → required checks never go green →
nothing merges → nothing breaks.

---

## Authentication — do this first, once

`/` and `/api/*` are locked to Google Workspace SSO. **A bare `curl` against
`/api/*` returns 401 or 503, and older runbooks that show unauthenticated curl
are wrong.** Browser cookies do not reach a bash process and the VS Code token
lives in the OS keychain, so terminal callers mint their own:

1. Open `$ENGINE_URL/auth/login?redirect=cli` in a browser and sign in.
2. Follow that endpoint's login flow. Save the resulting token privately in an endpoint-specific file with mode 600; set `SFDE_TOKEN_FILE` to its absolute path. Never paste a token into chat.
3. Re-run that login when a call reports 401. The token lasts 30 days.

`scripts/engine.sh` reads only the explicit `SFDE_TOKEN_FILE` (or `SFDE_TOKEN`) and sends
`Authorization: Bearer`. No default token file is read. Confirm the token and endpoint belong to the same authorized account. Use the helper rather than hand-rolled curl — the release and
rollback payloads are the fiddly part.

```bash
export ENGINE_URL=$(grep '^engine_url:' pipeline.yml | awk '{print $2}')
scripts/engine.sh status
```

**Everything 503s but `/health`?** In always-on that is the SSO gate failing
*closed* because `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` /
`SESSION_SECRET` are unset on the service. That is a provisioning fix, not an
auth fix. Under `EXECUTION_MODE=scale-to-zero` a different set of endpoints 503s
by design — see [references/provisioning.md](references/provisioning.md).

---

## Daily operations

The command examples use synthetic ticket keys, branch names and sandbox labels. Resolve actual values from the authorized project configuration; examples do not identify an account or grant access.

Full payloads, response shapes and every endpoint:
[references/operations.md](references/operations.md).

### Where does everything stand

```bash
scripts/engine.sh status          # FSM state, in-flight item and queue per env
scripts/doctor.sh                 # the same, plus tag drift, config drift, auth, webhook health
```

`SETTLED` idle · `DEPLOYING` in progress · `FROZEN` failed, waiting on a human.

### What is ready to ship

```bash
scripts/doctor.sh --ready         # unpromoted merge commits per promotion edge
```

Promotions are cherry-picks, so a promoted merge gets a new SHA downstream and
`git log main..preprod` reports it as pending forever. This compares by
**patch-equivalence** of each merge's first-parent diff, which is what actually
drops shipped work off the list.

### Promote

Bulk, everything on the upstream branch:

```bash
gh pr create --base main --head preprod --title "RELEASE: preprod -> main ($(date +%F))"
```

Merge commit, never squash. Never delete the upstream branch.

Selective, specific tickets — this is what the dashboard's release builder does:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh release --from preprod GH-397 GH-401 EXAMPLE-42
```

Ticket identifiers are provider-aware: `GH-397`, a Jira key like `EXAMPLE-42`, the
canonical `jira:EXAMPLE-42`, or a bare issue number. An identifier no **configured**
provider recognises is rejected rather than guessed at.

One release can span several sources — different dev sandboxes, or a sandbox and
preprod together. `--from` applies to every ticket after it, until the next one:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh release --to preprod --from sandbox-a GH-397 --from sandbox-b GH-401
```

**`--from` is required** — there is no default source, and the API rejects a flat
ticket list without one. `--to` *is* optional: it defaults to the target every
selected source agrees on, and with no shared target the request is refused
rather than one being picked.

Two refusals worth recognising, both deliberate:

- *"No merged PR delivering GH-397 found on \<src\>"* — a release cherry-picks
  merge commits. Work pushed straight to a branch shows on the board (which reads
  commit messages) but is not releasable until it lands as a merge.
- An **unattributed commit** check fails the release when a candidate merge
  carries work no selected ticket accounts for. That is the ride-along guard;
  read what it names before overriding.

### Roll back

```bash
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --ticket GH-397        # resolves the deploy that carried it
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --sha <merge-commit>   # or name the merge yourself
```

`--mode pr` (default) opens a revert PR so the inverse deployment is validated
first. `--mode direct` pushes the revert straight to the branch — emergencies
only. `git revert -m 1` produces a diff sgd turns into the exact inverse package:
modified components at prior versions in `package.xml`, added components in
`destructiveChanges.xml`.

**Re-land pattern:** never reuse the original branch. New branch, `git revert
<revert-sha>`, add the fix, new PR.

### Re-validate a PR

```bash
scripts/engine.sh revalidate --pr 412
```

Re-runs validation at the PR's live head SHA, clears the recorded failure and
bypasses the attempt cap — a human asking is explicit intent. This replaces the
old empty-commit workaround.

### Recover a freeze

```bash
scripts/engine.sh status                  # read freezeReason first
scripts/engine.sh retry preprod           # re-enqueue the deploy at branch HEAD
```

Retry only works on a `FROZEN` environment. If the cause is bad metadata rather
than a transient failure, roll back instead of retrying into the same wall.

### Pause for maintenance

Only when git has to be reconciled to the org by hand:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh pause
git tag -f deployed/main <sha> && git push origin deployed/main --force
scripts/engine.sh resume
```

Webhooks are acknowledged but not processed while paused. Tell the team — a
paused engine looks exactly like a quiet one.

---

## What the engine reacts to

| GitHub event | Engine reaction |
|---|---|
| `pull_request` opened/synchronize → env branch | Enqueue validation |
| `push` to env branch | Enqueue deploy |
| `pull_request` closed unmerged | Cancel queued validations; abandon an in-flight one, discarding its result |
| `pull_request` reopened | Re-enqueue validation |
| Issue label `express` | Auto-merge after validation, auto-promote after deploy |
| Label `qa:passed` / `qa:failed` | Update board state |
| Label `destructive-approved` | Satisfies the destructive gate |
| Label `run-tests` | Forces tests even when smart-test skip would apply |
| Route entry label | Permits a direct PR into a gated entry point |

**Labels the engine writes are write-only.** `env:*`, `deploy:failed` and
`rolled-back` exist so a human browsing GitHub can see where things are; the
engine never reads them back as truth. Delivery state comes from the event log.
The labels above that express **human intent** are read, and should be.

### Test level per tier

- **Pipeline environments** — the configured `test_level`, usually
  `RunLocalTests`, downgraded to `NoTestRun` only when `smart_tests` proves the
  whole delta is safe metadata. No partial trust: provably safe, or the full suite.
- **Production** — Salesforce forbids `NoTestRun` outright. Batch promotions into
  releases so N tickets cost one 15-minute run instead of N of them.

`smart_tests` never applies to a `production: true` environment, and any unsafe
type in the delta (ApexClass, CustomObject, Flow, LWC) means full tests. Config
and the safe-type list: [references/pipeline-config.md](references/pipeline-config.md).

---

## Route topology

`routes:` replaced `promotions:`. A config with only `promotions:` still loads —
it is translated into a synthetic `standard` route and warns — but it cannot
express hotfix entry points or back-merge, so migrate it.

- A **forward edge** is a consecutive pair on any route's `path`. Promote-only,
  by cherry-pick or PR. The union of all forward edges must be acyclic.
- **`entry_requires_label`** gates direct PRs into a route's entry point. Engine-owned
  head branches (`release/`, `express/`, `backmerge/`, `revert/`) and bulk
  promotion from an upstream env's branch are exempt — the gate only catches a
  fresh direct entry, which is exactly the hotfix case it exists for.
- **`back_merge`** targets fire after a successful deploy to a route's terminal
  env and must be strictly upstream, so a back-merge can never introduce a
  forward promotion path.

Full semantics and worked configs:
[references/pipeline-config.md](references/pipeline-config.md).

---

## Pre/post-deploy Apex hooks

Repo-versioned anonymous Apex the engine runs **around** a deploy, for imperative
org actions metadata cannot express. Off unless `deploy_hooks.enabled`.

```
deploy-hooks/
  pre/   01-disable-automation.apex
  post/  123-delete-orphan-flow-versions.apex
```

Scripts live outside `force-app/` so sgd never treats them as metadata. They are
**delta-driven and run-once**: discovered from the same `deployed/<branch>` → SHA
window as metadata, so a script appears in exactly one deploy's window. Add it in
the same PR as the change it supports.

```
compute delta → gates → [PRE] → sf deploy → [POST] → advance tag
```

The tag advances **last** — it means "org fully reconciled, hooks included." A
pre-hook failure freezes with nothing deployed. A post-hook failure freezes with
the tag **not** advanced, so Retry re-runs deploy + post: **write hooks
idempotently.** Hooks never run during validation — anonymous Apex has no
`checkOnly`, so a hooks-only PR validates trivially green and then runs its
scripts on merge with no metadata deploy at all.

---

## Ticket providers

Absent `tickets:` means GitHub only, exactly as before providers existed.

- `extract` — regexes over commit and PR text. Free, read-only. Once a tracker
  has ever been used, leave it on permanently: commits written in that period
  name its tickets forever.
- `board` — the kanban's card source, and a **credentialed** read when it
  includes `jira`. Validated at config load; the engine refuses to start without
  `base_url`, `email` and `projects`, because the failure it prevents is a board
  rendering with every Jira card silently missing, which reads as "nothing to
  ship."

`projects` is load-bearing: the Jira key regex is built from the allowlist, never
from the general key shape, because `/[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+/` also matches `UTF-8`
and `ISO-8601`. No allowlist, no Jira extraction. The token never appears in
`pipeline.yml` — mount `JIRA_API_TOKEN` from Secret Manager.

---

## Key rules

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Pipeline environments are the engine's, exclusively | A manual deploy desyncs `deployed/<branch>` with no way for the engine to detect it |
| Merge commits everywhere, never squash | `git revert -m 1` and `git cherry-pick -m 1` both need real merge commits |
| Never move `deployed/<branch>` unless paused | The tag is the engine's statement about the org |
| A `pipeline.yml` change is not live until the engine restarts | Config is read once at bootstrap; merging it is necessary, not sufficient |
| Mint a CLI token; never expect bare curl to work | `/api/*` is behind Workspace SSO |
| Release by ticket, not by SHA, when you can | The ticket → deploy join is what the model exists for, and it catches ride-alongs |
| Batch production promotions | `NoTestRun` is illegal in production, so every promotion costs a full test run |
| Never `--use-most-recent` on any `sf` command | Another deploy — yours, another agent's, or the engine's — may be the most recent |
| Deploy hooks must be idempotent | A Retry re-runs them; a post-hook freeze re-runs the whole deploy + post |
| Loosen quick-deploy eligibility only with a false-positive argument | A false negative costs 30 minutes; a false positive ships untested metadata |
| Engine down = frozen line, and that is correct | Required checks never go green, so nothing merges |

---

## Known gaps

Verify against the engine repo's issue list rather than trusting this section to
be current.

- **Failure-path drills have never been run** (engine repo #4): freeze, rollback,
  sequencing, re-land and kill. The paths are implemented and unit-tested; they
  have not been exercised against a real org under failure.
- **Scale-to-zero has never run against a real org.** Every timing constant is
  reasoned, not observed. Read the known-risk list before enabling it.
- **`Deploy.contentHash` exists and nothing populates it** — quick deploy is
  still SHA-based.

---

## Troubleshooting

[references/troubleshooting.md](references/troubleshooting.md) — symptom to
action, including the two different families of 503, a board that renders empty,
config that appears not to apply, and webhook silence.

## Related skills

- **`sf-delivery-standards`** — everything below the environment branch: the
  ticket, the worktree, the local dry run, the sandbox deploy, the hooks. Run its
  `init` on an engine-managed repo with `trunk` set to the dev sandbox branch;
  nothing else about it needs to change for the engine.

  There is exactly **one** point of contact, and it is a value in this repo's git
  config using that skill's own documented key: its merge gate defaults to
  `estate.squash=require`, which would refuse the merge commits promotion and
  rollback depend on, so `scripts/init.sh` sets it to the existing `prefer` value
  and lets the engine's own guard enforce merge-commits-only. No code in that
  skill changes, and nobody working the local loop has to do anything.
- **`/simplify`** — the AI quality gate, before any commit.

Full payloads, response shapes and every endpoint: references/operations.md (references/operations.md).

Where does everything stand

scripts/engine.sh status          # FSM state, in-flight item and queue per env
scripts/doctor.sh                 # the same, plus tag drift, config drift, auth, webhook health

SETTLED idle · DEPLOYING in progress · FROZEN failed, waiting on a human.

What is ready to ship

scripts/doctor.sh --ready         # unpromoted merge commits per promotion edge

Promotions are cherry-picks, so a promoted merge gets a new SHA downstream and git log main..preprod reports it as pending forever. This compares by patch-equivalence of each merge's first-parent diff, which is what actually drops shipped work off the list.

Promote

Bulk, everything on the upstream branch:

gh pr create --base main --head preprod --title "RELEASE: preprod -> main ($(date +%F))"

Merge commit, never squash. Never delete the upstream branch.

Selective, specific tickets — this is what the dashboard's release builder does:

scripts/engine.sh release --from preprod GH-397 GH-401 EXAMPLE-42

Ticket identifiers are provider-aware: GH-397, a Jira key like EXAMPLE-42, the canonical jira:EXAMPLE-42, or a bare issue number. An identifier no configured provider recognises is rejected rather than guessed at.

One release can span several sources — different dev sandboxes, or a sandbox and preprod together. --from applies to every ticket after it, until the next one:

scripts/engine.sh release --to preprod --from sandbox-a GH-397 --from sandbox-b GH-401

--from is required — there is no default source, and the API rejects a flat ticket list without one. --to *is* optional: it defaults to the target every selected source agrees on, and with no shared target the request is refused rather than one being picked.

Two refusals worth recognising, both deliberate:

  • *"No merged PR delivering GH-397 found on \<src\>"* — a release cherry-picks

merge commits. Work pushed straight to a branch shows on the board (which reads commit messages) but is not releasable until it lands as a merge.

  • An unattributed commit check fails the release when a candidate merge

carries work no selected ticket accounts for. That is the ride-along guard; read what it names before overriding.

Roll back

scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --ticket GH-397        # resolves the deploy that carried it
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --sha <merge-commit>   # or name the merge yourself

--mode pr (default) opens a revert PR so the inverse deployment is validated first. --mode direct pushes the revert straight to the branch — emergencies only. git revert -m 1 produces a diff sgd turns into the exact inverse package: modified components at prior versions in package.xml, added components in destructiveChanges.xml.

Re-land pattern: never reuse the original branch. New branch, git revert <revert-sha>, add the fix, new PR.

Re-validate a PR

scripts/engine.sh revalidate --pr 412

Re-runs validation at the PR's live head SHA, clears the recorded failure and bypasses the attempt cap — a human asking is explicit intent. This replaces the old empty-commit workaround.

Recover a freeze

scripts/engine.sh status                  # read freezeReason first
scripts/engine.sh retry preprod           # re-enqueue the deploy at branch HEAD

Retry only works on a FROZEN environment. If the cause is bad metadata rather than a transient failure, roll back instead of retrying into the same wall.

Pause for maintenance

Only when git has to be reconciled to the org by hand:

scripts/engine.sh pause
git tag -f deployed/main <sha> && git push origin deployed/main --force
scripts/engine.sh resume

Webhooks are acknowledged but not processed while paused. Tell the team — a paused engine looks exactly like a quiet one.

---

What the engine reacts to

GitHub eventEngine reaction
pull_request opened/synchronize → env branchEnqueue validation
push to env branchEnqueue deploy
pull_request closed unmergedCancel queued validations; abandon an in-flight one, discarding its result
pull_request reopenedRe-enqueue validation
Issue label expressAuto-merge after validation, auto-promote after deploy
Label qa:passed / qa:failedUpdate board state
Label destructive-approvedSatisfies the destructive gate
Label run-testsForces tests even when smart-test skip would apply
Route entry labelPermits a direct PR into a gated entry point

Labels the engine writes are write-only. env:*, deploy:failed and rolled-back exist so a human browsing GitHub can see where things are; the engine never reads them back as truth. Delivery state comes from the event log. The labels above that express human intent are read, and should be.

Test level per tier

  • Pipeline environments — the configured test_level, usually

RunLocalTests, downgraded to NoTestRun only when smart_tests proves the whole delta is safe metadata. No partial trust: provably safe, or the full suite.

  • Production — Salesforce forbids NoTestRun outright. Batch promotions into

releases so N tickets cost one 15-minute run instead of N of them.

smart_tests never applies to a production: true environment, and any unsafe type in the delta (ApexClass, CustomObject, Flow, LWC) means full tests. Config and the safe-type list: references/pipeline-config.md (references/pipeline-config.md).

---

Route topology

routes: replaced promotions:. A config with only promotions: still loads — it is translated into a synthetic standard route and warns — but it cannot express hotfix entry points or back-merge, so migrate it.

  • A forward edge is a consecutive pair on any route's path. Promote-only,

by cherry-pick or PR. The union of all forward edges must be acyclic.

  • entry_requires_label gates direct PRs into a route's entry point. Engine-owned

head branches (release/, express/, backmerge/, revert/) and bulk promotion from an upstream env's branch are exempt — the gate only catches a fresh direct entry, which is exactly the hotfix case it exists for.

  • back_merge targets fire after a successful deploy to a route's terminal

env and must be strictly upstream, so a back-merge can never introduce a forward promotion path.

Full semantics and worked configs: references/pipeline-config.md (references/pipeline-config.md).

---

Pre/post-deploy Apex hooks

Repo-versioned anonymous Apex the engine runs around a deploy, for imperative org actions metadata cannot express. Off unless deploy_hooks.enabled.

deploy-hooks/
  pre/   01-disable-automation.apex
  post/  123-delete-orphan-flow-versions.apex

Scripts live outside force-app/ so sgd never treats them as metadata. They are delta-driven and run-once: discovered from the same deployed/<branch> → SHA window as metadata, so a script appears in exactly one deploy's window. Add it in the same PR as the change it supports.

compute delta → gates → [PRE] → sf deploy → [POST] → advance tag

The tag advances last — it means "org fully reconciled, hooks included." A pre-hook failure freezes with nothing deployed. A post-hook failure freezes with the tag not advanced, so Retry re-runs deploy + post: write hooks idempotently. Hooks never run during validation — anonymous Apex has no checkOnly, so a hooks-only PR validates trivially green and then runs its scripts on merge with no metadata deploy at all.

---

Ticket providers

Absent tickets: means GitHub only, exactly as before providers existed.

  • extract — regexes over commit and PR text. Free, read-only. Once a tracker

has ever been used, leave it on permanently: commits written in that period name its tickets forever.

  • board — the kanban's card source, and a credentialed read when it

includes jira. Validated at config load; the engine refuses to start without base_url, email and projects, because the failure it prevents is a board rendering with every Jira card silently missing, which reads as "nothing to ship."

projects is load-bearing: the Jira key regex is built from the allowlist, never from the general key shape, because /[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+/ also matches UTF-8 and ISO-8601. No allowlist, no Jira extraction. The token never appears in pipeline.yml — mount JIRA_API_TOKEN from Secret Manager.

---

Key rules

RuleWhy
Pipeline environments are the engine's, exclusivelyA manual deploy desyncs deployed/<branch> with no way for the engine to detect it
Merge commits everywhere, never squashgit revert -m 1 and git cherry-pick -m 1 both need real merge commits
Never move deployed/<branch> unless pausedThe tag is the engine's statement about the org
A pipeline.yml change is not live until the engine restartsConfig is read once at bootstrap; merging it is necessary, not sufficient
Mint a CLI token; never expect bare curl to work/api/* is behind Workspace SSO
Release by ticket, not by SHA, when you canThe ticket → deploy join is what the model exists for, and it catches ride-alongs
Batch production promotionsNoTestRun is illegal in production, so every promotion costs a full test run
Never --use-most-recent on any sf commandAnother deploy — yours, another agent's, or the engine's — may be the most recent
Deploy hooks must be idempotentA Retry re-runs them; a post-hook freeze re-runs the whole deploy + post
Loosen quick-deploy eligibility only with a false-positive argumentA false negative costs 30 minutes; a false positive ships untested metadata
Engine down = frozen line, and that is correctRequired checks never go green, so nothing merges

---

Known gaps

Verify against the engine repo's issue list rather than trusting this section to be current.

  • Failure-path drills have never been run (engine repo #4): freeze, rollback,

sequencing, re-land and kill. The paths are implemented and unit-tested; they have not been exercised against a real org under failure.

  • Scale-to-zero has never run against a real org. Every timing constant is

reasoned, not observed. Read the known-risk list before enabling it.

  • Deploy.contentHash exists and nothing populates it — quick deploy is

still SHA-based.

---

Troubleshooting

references/troubleshooting.md (references/troubleshooting.md) — symptom to action, including the two different families of 503, a board that renders empty, config that appears not to apply, and webhook silence.

Related skills

  • sf-delivery-standards — everything below the environment branch: the

ticket, the worktree, the local dry run, the sandbox deploy, the hooks. Run its init on an engine-managed repo with trunk set to the dev sandbox branch; nothing else about it needs to change for the engine.

There is exactly one point of contact, and it is a value in this repo's git config using that skill's own documented key: its merge gate defaults to estate.squash=require, which would refuse the merge commits promotion and rollback depend on, so scripts/init.sh sets it to the existing prefer value and lets the engine's own guard enforce merge-commits-only. No code in that skill changes, and nobody working the local loop has to do anything.

  • /simplify — the AI quality gate, before any commit.

The engine is an always-on orchestrator that owns Salesforce deployments to pipeline environments through GitHub webhooks, one single-threaded FSM worker per environment, and strict git-to-org synchronization. It takes over at the first environment branch and owns everything upward.

This skill starts at the PR into an environment branch. Everything before that — the ticket, the worktree, the local dry run, the deploy to your own dev sandbox, the git and agent lifecycle hooks that enforce it — is sf-delivery-standards, and that skill works the same whether or not an engine sits above it. Do not duplicate its rules here and do not answer local-loop questions from this skill.

This is a layer, not a fork. The engine ships its own two guards (scripts/init.sh installs them), which read pipeline.yml and nothing else. They add refusals on top of the local-loop stack, read none of its config, and write none of its files. An agent working the local loop needs to know nothing about this layer and change nothing to accommodate it. If you find yourself about to edit sf-delivery-standards to make something here work, stop — that is the seam being crossed, and the answer is a rule in this skill's own hooks.

  canon_exempt_reason: 'Enforcement-stack reference an agent must hold in full: rule IDs, exit codes, suppression contract, and engine semantics, punctuation included.'
---


# Salesforce Enterprise Patterns (Estate House Architecture)

This skill does two things: it tells you **how to structure Salesforce code** the house way,
and it ships **scripted checks** (`scripts/arch_check.py`) that verify the structure
mechanically — runnable ad hoc, in CI, or as a git pre-commit hook with warn/block modes.

Why this architecture exists (short version): business logic in one place (services) so
trigger, UI, and API paths never diverge; DML in one place (Unit of Work) so transaction
ordering and partial-save behavior are deliberate; SOQL in one place (selectors) so
field-level security is enforced by default and query shape is reviewable; DTOs at the UI
boundary so the LWC/React view layer is decoupled from the data model. The full spec with
code examples is in `references/architecture.md` — read it before writing code in an
unfamiliar layer. The rule catalog with rationale per check is in `references/rules.md`.

## Project adoption

This is a reusable reference architecture, not an employer or platform mandate. Read the project's architecture decisions and existing framework before applying it. Preserve a confirmed project convention unless the user authorizes migration. If adoption is undecided, present compatibility findings and leave enforcement uninstalled. The bundled rule severities are defaults for this named pattern, not policies inferred for a new client.

## The layers at a glance

| Layer | Naming | Owns | Never contains |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trigger | `<Object>.trigger` | One dispatch line to its handler | Logic, SOQL, DML, loops, ifs |
| Trigger handler | `<Object>TriggerHandler.cls` | Context routing, recursion guard | SOQL, DML (delegates to services) |
| Service | `<Domain>Service.cls` | Business logic, bulk-first, transaction boundaries | UI shaping, direct SOQL |
| Selector | `<Object>sSelector.cls` | ALL SOQL for its object, `WITH USER_MODE` | DML, business logic |
| Unit of Work | `UnitOfWork.cls` (shipped) | ALL DML, ordered commit | Queries, logic |
| Controller | `<Feature>Controller.cls` | `@AuraEnabled` entry points, DTO mapping, error translation | Business logic, SOQL, DML |
| DTO | `<Feature>DTO.cls` or inner classes | `@AuraEnabled` plain properties | SObject fields, logic |
| LWC | `<feature>/` | View logic, **imperative** Apex calls | `@wire` to Apex (LDS ui*Api wires are fine) |

A UI request flows: LWC → imperative call → Controller → Service → Selector (reads) /
UnitOfWork (writes) → Controller maps result to DTO → LWC. A trigger flows: Trigger →
Handler → the same Service. That shared middle is the entire point.

**Handler-layer variant:** the trigger dispatch layer is swappable. The default is the
shipped `TriggerHandler.cls`; orgs with meaningful Flow + Apex automation mix (or
multi-team automation on shared objects) should use the Trigger Actions Framework instead —
read `references/taf.md` before scaffolding trigger work in a repo that uses TAF (you'll
see `MetadataTriggerHandler` in triggers and `Trigger_Action__mdt` metadata). All other
layers and all checker rules are identical under both.

## Scaffolding a new feature

1. Copy the base classes from `assets/apex/` into the target repo if not already present:
   `UnitOfWork.cls`, `TriggerHandler.cls` (plus their `-meta.xml` files — generate matching
   the repo's existing API version). These are lean and owned — do not substitute fflib.
2. Create the selector before the service. Every SOQL statement it contains uses
   `WITH USER_MODE` (or `AccessLevel.USER_MODE` for `Database.query*`). System-mode queries
   require an inline `// ARCH-EXEMPT: APX003 <reason>` and a real reason.
3. Write the service bulk-first: every public method takes collections, even if today's only
   caller passes one record. Services receive or construct a `UnitOfWork`, register changes,
   and either commit it or hand it back to the caller who owns the transaction.
4. Controllers are thin: try/catch translating exceptions to `AuraHandledException`, calls
   into the service, maps SObjects to DTOs. Mark read methods `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`
   when semantics allow — imperative calls still hit the client cache.
5. LWC calls Apex imperatively (`import method from '@salesforce/apex/...'` then `await`).
   If an imperative write touches records shown elsewhere on a Lightning page, call
   `notifyRecordUpdateAvailable()` so standard components don't go stale. LDS wire adapters
   (`lightning/uiRecordApi` etc.) and record forms remain the right tool for plainly
   record-centric display/edit — don't force the DTO ceremony onto those.
6. Follow the code examples in `references/architecture.md` for each file you create.

## Running the checks

```bash
python3 scripts/arch_check.py --paths force-app/           # whole tree
python3 scripts/arch_check.py --staged                     # staged files only (hook mode)
python3 scripts/arch_check.py --paths force-app/ --json    # machine-readable
```

Exit code 0 = clean or warnings only; 1 = at least one blocking violation; 2 = usage/config
error. Run the checker after writing or modifying Apex/LWC and fix (or consciously exempt)
findings before presenting work as done.

### Engines: PMD-first, regex fallback

arch_check is an orchestrator with two engines. The **pmd** engine runs the custom PMD 7
ruleset at `assets/pmd/estate-apex.xml` (AST-accurate, and the same rules a dev's IDE
and CI see via the org's PMD standards), then applies the policy PMD can't express:
warn/block modes, legacy-path downgrades, exclude paths, and suppression governance. The
**regex** engine is the self-contained fallback for environments without PMD — no
dependencies, same rule IDs, slightly less precise. Default `--engine auto` picks pmd when
a PMD binary is found (config `pmdPath`, `$PMD_BIN`, or `pmd` on PATH). The LWC rule
(LWC001) always runs in the wrapper; for in-editor feedback there's also an ESLint version
at `assets/eslint/no-wire-of-apex.js` (PMD cannot parse modern LWC JavaScript).

Suppression policy, in order of preference: (1) `@SuppressWarnings('PMD.RuleName')` with a
trailing `// reason` comment — silences PMD everywhere including the IDE; (2) `// NOPMD -
reason` for one line; (3) `// ARCH-EXEMPT: APX003 reason` — wrapper-level, works under
both engines. A suppression without a reason is itself a blocking violation (META001 for
ARCH-EXEMPT, META002 for the PMD forms): for AI-generated code the reason string is the
audit trail, and an agent that adds one must tell the user it did and why.

### Configuration: `.arch-check.json` at the repo root

Copy `assets/arch-check.json` as a starting point:

```json
{
  "mode": "block",
  "legacyPaths": ["force-app/main/default/classes/legacy/**"],
  "rules": { "APX004": "warn", "LWC001": "warn" },
  "dmlAllowlist": ["UnitOfWork"],
  "exemptTestClasses": true
}
```

- `mode`: repo-wide default — `block` (violations fail the commit) or `warn` (report only).
  New engagements start at `block`; use `warn` when adopting the pattern on an existing
  codebase you haven't refactored yet.
- `legacyPaths`: globs for old code. Findings in matching files are downgraded to warn no
  matter what — new work stays blocked, old work stays visible without stopping commits.
  As legacy code gets refactored, shrink these globs.
- `rules`: per-rule override — `"off"`, `"warn"`, or `"block"`. Rule IDs are in
  `references/rules.md`.
- `dmlAllowlist`: class names (without `.cls`) allowed to perform raw DML besides
  `UnitOfWork`. Keep it short; every entry is a hole in the transaction story.
- `excludePaths`: globs skipped entirely — for vendored third-party framework source
  (e.g. a vendored Trigger Actions Framework). First-party code never goes here.
- `exemptTestClasses`: `@IsTest` files skip placement rules (they still shouldn't rot, but
  test setup legitimately does raw DML and SOQL).

### Inline exemptions

Any finding can be suppressed on a specific line with a trailing or preceding comment:

```apex
List<User> admins = [SELECT Id FROM User WITH SYSTEM_MODE]; // ARCH-EXEMPT: APX003 admin audit runs as system by design
```

An exemption without a reason after the rule ID is itself a violation (`META001`). Exemptions
are for genuine exceptions, not for finishing faster — when you add one while working on a
task, tell the user you did and why.

### Enforcement: two installation paths

**Repo already running the Estate delivery-standards stack** (sf-delivery-standards;
you'll see `git config core.hooksPath` pointing at `~/.estate/githooks`): do NOT install
a `.git/hooks` hook — it would never fire. That stack's pre-commit gate 4 runs PMD against
`config/pmd-ruleset.xml`, so integration is one file: copy
`assets/pmd/estate-apex.xml` to `config/estate-apex.xml` and
`assets/pmd/pmd-ruleset-project.xml` to `config/pmd-ruleset.xml` (or merge the
architecture rule refs into an existing project ruleset). The architecture rules are then
blocking under `git config estate.pmd block`, advisory under `advise` — that knob is the
delivery stack's warn/block equivalent. Add the ESLint rule to the repo's eslint config so
gate 3 covers LWC001, and run `arch_check.py` in CI (or an npm script) for what PMD can't
express: legacy-path downgrades and suppression-reason governance.
`scripts/install_hooks.py` detects this stack and prints these steps instead of writing an
inert hook.

**Standalone repo** (no delivery-standards stack):

```bash
python3 scripts/install_hooks.py            # writes .git/hooks/pre-commit + copies ruleset
python3 scripts/install_hooks.py --print    # just print the hook (for husky users)
```

The hook runs `arch_check.py --staged` against staged file *content* (not the working
tree), so partially-staged files are checked as they'll actually be committed. Bypass in an
emergency with `git commit --no-verify` — but treat that as a flag to raise, not a habit.

## Rules the checker enforces

| ID | Default | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| APX001 | block | SOQL/SOSL outside `*Selector` classes |
| APX002 | block | DML outside `UnitOfWork` (+ configured allowlist) |
| APX003 | block | Selector SOQL missing `USER_MODE`/`SECURITY_ENFORCED` |
| APX004 | warn | `@AuraEnabled` method returns SObject types instead of DTOs |
| APX005 | block | Logic in trigger bodies (anything beyond handler dispatch) |
| APX006 | warn | Public service methods taking a single SObject (bulk-first smell) |
| APX007 | warn | Generic collections nested 3+ levels (extract a named class) |
| LWC001 | warn | `@wire` on an `@salesforce/apex` import (should be imperative) |
| META001 | block | `ARCH-EXEMPT` without a rule ID and reason |
| META002 | block | `@SuppressWarnings`/`NOPMD` without a reason comment |

Full rationale, examples, and remediation per rule: `references/rules.md`. When a finding is
a false positive you can't restructure around, exempt it inline with a reason — never
disable a whole rule to silence one line.

## Reviewing existing code

When asked to review code against this architecture (not just write it), run the checker
first for the mechanical findings, then read `references/architecture.md` and look for what
scripts can't see: services that shape UI responses, transaction ownership ambiguity (who
commits the UoW?), selectors leaking query building into callers, controllers with business
logic that happens to contain no SOQL/DML. Report scripted findings and judgment findings
separately.

caller passes one record. Services receive or construct a UnitOfWork, register changes, and either commit it or hand it back to the caller who owns the transaction.

  1. Controllers are thin: try/catch translating exceptions to AuraHandledException, calls

into the service, maps SObjects to DTOs. Mark read methods @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) when semantics allow — imperative calls still hit the client cache.

  1. LWC calls Apex imperatively (import method from '@salesforce/apex/...' then await).

If an imperative write touches records shown elsewhere on a Lightning page, call notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() so standard components don't go stale. LDS wire adapters (lightning/uiRecordApi etc.) and record forms remain the right tool for plainly record-centric display/edit — don't force the DTO ceremony onto those.

  1. Follow the code examples in references/architecture.md for each file you create.

Running the checks

python3 scripts/arch_check.py --paths force-app/           # whole tree
python3 scripts/arch_check.py --staged                     # staged files only (hook mode)
python3 scripts/arch_check.py --paths force-app/ --json    # machine-readable

Exit code 0 = clean or warnings only; 1 = at least one blocking violation; 2 = usage/config error. Run the checker after writing or modifying Apex/LWC and fix (or consciously exempt) findings before presenting work as done.

Engines: PMD-first, regex fallback

arch_check is an orchestrator with two engines. The pmd engine runs the custom PMD 7 ruleset at assets/pmd/estate-apex.xml (AST-accurate, and the same rules a dev's IDE and CI see via the org's PMD standards), then applies the policy PMD can't express: warn/block modes, legacy-path downgrades, exclude paths, and suppression governance. The regex engine is the self-contained fallback for environments without PMD — no dependencies, same rule IDs, slightly less precise. Default --engine auto picks pmd when a PMD binary is found (config pmdPath, $PMD_BIN, or pmd on PATH). The LWC rule (LWC001) always runs in the wrapper; for in-editor feedback there's also an ESLint version at assets/eslint/no-wire-of-apex.js (PMD cannot parse modern LWC JavaScript).

Suppression policy, in order of preference: (1) @SuppressWarnings('PMD.RuleName') with a trailing // reason comment — silences PMD everywhere including the IDE; (2) // NOPMD - reason for one line; (3) // ARCH-EXEMPT: APX003 reason — wrapper-level, works under both engines. A suppression without a reason is itself a blocking violation (META001 for ARCH-EXEMPT, META002 for the PMD forms): for AI-generated code the reason string is the audit trail, and an agent that adds one must tell the user it did and why.

Configuration: .arch-check.json at the repo root

Copy assets/arch-check.json as a starting point:

{
  "mode": "block",
  "legacyPaths": ["force-app/main/default/classes/legacy/**"],
  "rules": { "APX004": "warn", "LWC001": "warn" },
  "dmlAllowlist": ["UnitOfWork"],
  "exemptTestClasses": true
}
  • mode: repo-wide default — block (violations fail the commit) or warn (report only).

New engagements start at block; use warn when adopting the pattern on an existing codebase you haven't refactored yet.

  • legacyPaths: globs for old code. Findings in matching files are downgraded to warn no

matter what — new work stays blocked, old work stays visible without stopping commits. As legacy code gets refactored, shrink these globs.

  • rules: per-rule override — "off", "warn", or "block". Rule IDs are in

references/rules.md.

  • dmlAllowlist: class names (without .cls) allowed to perform raw DML besides

UnitOfWork. Keep it short; every entry is a hole in the transaction story.

  • excludePaths: globs skipped entirely — for vendored third-party framework source

(e.g. a vendored Trigger Actions Framework). First-party code never goes here.

  • exemptTestClasses: @IsTest files skip placement rules (they still shouldn't rot, but

test setup legitimately does raw DML and SOQL).

Inline exemptions

Any finding can be suppressed on a specific line with a trailing or preceding comment:

List<User> admins = [SELECT Id FROM User WITH SYSTEM_MODE]; // ARCH-EXEMPT: APX003 admin audit runs as system by design

An exemption without a reason after the rule ID is itself a violation (META001). Exemptions are for genuine exceptions, not for finishing faster — when you add one while working on a task, tell the user you did and why.

Enforcement: two installation paths

Repo already running the Estate delivery-standards stack (sf-delivery-standards; you'll see git config core.hooksPath pointing at ~/.estate/githooks): do NOT install a .git/hooks hook — it would never fire. That stack's pre-commit gate 4 runs PMD against config/pmd-ruleset.xml, so integration is one file: copy assets/pmd/estate-apex.xml to config/estate-apex.xml and assets/pmd/pmd-ruleset-project.xml to config/pmd-ruleset.xml (or merge the architecture rule refs into an existing project ruleset). The architecture rules are then blocking under git config estate.pmd block, advisory under advise — that knob is the delivery stack's warn/block equivalent. Add the ESLint rule to the repo's eslint config so gate 3 covers LWC001, and run arch_check.py in CI (or an npm script) for what PMD can't express: legacy-path downgrades and suppression-reason governance. scripts/install_hooks.py detects this stack and prints these steps instead of writing an inert hook.

Standalone repo (no delivery-standards stack):

python3 scripts/install_hooks.py            # writes .git/hooks/pre-commit + copies ruleset
python3 scripts/install_hooks.py --print    # just print the hook (for husky users)

The hook runs arch_check.py --staged against staged file *content* (not the working tree), so partially-staged files are checked as they'll actually be committed. Bypass in an emergency with git commit --no-verify — but treat that as a flag to raise, not a habit.

Rules the checker enforces

IDDefaultChecks
APX001blockSOQL/SOSL outside *Selector classes
APX002blockDML outside UnitOfWork (+ configured allowlist)
APX003blockSelector SOQL missing USER_MODE/SECURITY_ENFORCED
APX004warn@AuraEnabled method returns SObject types instead of DTOs
APX005blockLogic in trigger bodies (anything beyond handler dispatch)
APX006warnPublic service methods taking a single SObject (bulk-first smell)
APX007warnGeneric collections nested 3+ levels (extract a named class)
LWC001warn@wire on an @salesforce/apex import (should be imperative)
META001blockARCH-EXEMPT without a rule ID and reason
META002block@SuppressWarnings/NOPMD without a reason comment

Full rationale, examples, and remediation per rule: references/rules.md. When a finding is a false positive you can't restructure around, exempt it inline with a reason — never disable a whole rule to silence one line.

Reviewing existing code

When asked to review code against this architecture (not just write it), run the checker first for the mechanical findings, then read references/architecture.md and look for what scripts can't see: services that shape UI responses, transaction ownership ambiguity (who commits the UoW?), selectors leaking query building into callers, controllers with business logic that happens to contain no SOQL/DML. Report scripted findings and judgment findings separately.
skills.excerptHtml:
This skill does two things: it tells you how to structure Salesforce code the house way, and it ships scripted checks (scripts/arch_check.py) that verify the structure mechanically — runnable ad hoc, in CI, or as a git pre-commit hook with warn/block modes.

Why this architecture exists (short version): business logic in one place (services) so trigger, UI, and API paths never diverge; DML in one place (Unit of Work) so transaction ordering and partial-save behavior are deliberate; SOQL in one place (selectors) so field-level security is enforced by default and query shape is reviewable; DTOs at the UI boundary so the LWC/React view layer is decoupled from the data model. The full spec with code examples is in references/architecture.md — read it before writing code in an unfamiliar layer. The rule catalog with rationale per check is in references/rules.md.

This is a reusable reference architecture, not an employer or platform mandate. Read the project's architecture decisions and existing framework before applying it. Preserve a confirmed project convention unless the user authorizes migration. If adoption is undecided, present compatibility findings and leave enforcement uninstalled. The bundled rule severities are defaults for this named pattern, not policies inferred for a new client.

skills.markdown:
---
name: sf-headless-screenshot
description: 'Drive the sfqa CLI to capture headless screenshots and run clickpath assertions against a Salesforce org. No interactive login, no credential exposure. Trigger when you need to capture what a Salesforce page looks like without a human watching: after deploying UI-affecting metadata and needing verification evidence, when estate-ac-qa needs its browser driver, or when a ticket needs screenshot proof of a rendered page. Do not trigger for interactive browser exploration (use sf-browser-automation) or for non-Salesforce pages.'
---


# Salesforce Headless Screenshot

Captures real Lightning pages from a real headless Chromium, authenticated off
the SF CLI. No interactive login, no credential in the transcript.

**Tool:** set `SFQA_HOME` to the explicitly selected installation for this task.
Verify that its `sfqa.mjs` exists and inspect its current help before use. This
skill does not bundle that executable or establish that a cached installation is
approved. If no supported tool is available, report the browser check pending.

```bash
: "${SFQA_HOME:?Set SFQA_HOME to the selected tool installation}"
test -f "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs"
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" help
```

Use an explicitly confirmed org alias and page or record ID from the task.
The examples below are synthetic; replace their identifiers before invocation.
A write in a clickpath needs the user's authorization for that target.

## When to use this

Use this skill when you need a headless, unattended screenshot or clickpath
assertion against a Salesforce org. Typical callers:

- **`estate-ac-qa`** loads this as its Step 0 browser driver
- Any agent that needs visual evidence of a deployed change
- Manual requests for "show me the page" or "screenshot the record"

For interactive exploration in a visible Chrome the user is watching, use
`sf-browser-automation` instead. This skill is headless-only.

## First run

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" doctor            # checks SF CLI + Chromium
```

If Chromium is missing, report the dependency. Install a supported browser only when authorized. Do not launch installed macOS Chrome through Node or Playwright; use a permitted connected browser or supported isolated Chromium environment. Never retry the blocked launch path.

## Single screenshot

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" shot \
  --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS \
  --url /lightning/r/Account/ACCOUNT_RECORD_ID/view \
  --wait record \
  --out qa/GH-42/account.png --text
```

Writes `account.png`, `account.meta.json` (URL, title, readiness) and, with
`--text`, `account.txt` containing the page's visible text, which is what you
should grep to confirm a value rendered.

Prints a JSON receipt. **Check `ready`**: `false` means a readiness stage timed
out and the image may show a partly-loaded page.

## Many screenshots (one browser, one session)

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" batch --list shots.json
```

```json
{
  "org": "CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-42",
  "viewport": "1600x1000",
  "text": true,
  "shots": [
    { "name": "quote",    "url": "/lightning/r/Quote/0Q0.../view", "wait": "record", "fullPage": true },
    { "name": "accounts", "url": "/lightning/o/Account/list",      "wait": "list" },
    { "name": "fields",   "url": "/lightning/setup/ObjectManager/Account/FieldsAndRelationships/view" }
  ]
}
```

## Clickpath + acceptance criteria (the QA workhorse)

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" flow --flow acceptance.json
```

```json
{
  "org": "CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS",
  "name": "GH-42 invoice summary fees",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-42",
  "text": true,
  "steps": [
    { "goto": "/lightning/r/Account/001.../view", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": ["Account Health Summary", "Annual Revenue"], "shot": "details" },
    { "click": "a[role=\"tab\"]:has-text(\"Related\")", "shot": "related" },
    { "expectText": "Contacts" },
    { "click": "button:has-text(\"Edit\")", "wait": "edit", "shot": "edit-modal" },
    { "fill": { "selector": "input[name=\"Name\"]", "value": "Acme Corp" } },
    { "click": "button[name=\"SaveEdit\"]", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": "Acme Corp", "shot": "saved", "critical": true }
  ]
}
```

Writes numbered PNGs plus `report.json` and `report.md` (inline screenshots,
per-step pass/fail) into `outDir`. Exit code 2 if any step failed, so it works as
a gate. `report.md` pastes straight into a GitHub issue or PR comment.

**Step keys:** `goto`, `wait`, `waitFor`, `settle`, `quiet`, `dismiss`, `click`,
`clickAt`, `hover`, `type`, `fill`, `press`, `scroll`, `scrollTo`, `expectText`,
`expectNoText`, `shot`, `critical`, `name`.

## When to trust the detector, and when to use your own eyes

`shot`/`batch`/`flow` use readiness heuristics. Verify them against representative pages in the selected org before relying on a bulk capture; prior measurements from another org do not establish current readiness.

Use `watch` when a heuristic shouldn't have the final say, for example an LWC doing
an external callout that legitimately takes 20s, a page that looks wrong, or
anything unfamiliar:

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" watch --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS \
  --url /lightning/r/Account/001.../view --every 2000 --for 20000 --out-dir qa/watch
```

It captures a frame every N ms and **decides nothing**. Read the frames, judge
visually, and re-run with a larger `--for` if `stillMoving` is true.

## Slowness is a finding, report it

Every capture reports `renderMs` (when the page actually stopped changing, the QA
signal) and `totalMs` (includes ~3.9s of our own confirmation window). `slow: true`
appears when `renderMs` exceeds `--slow-threshold` (default 5000).

Treat a slow page as a defect worth mentioning, not just a longer wait. Likely
causes: slow SOQL, an external callout, or a stale LWC needing recompile. Retry
with `--hard-refresh` to rule the last one out.

**Calibrate per org.** Measure representative pages in the authorized target and
record the samples before selecting `--slow-threshold`. A threshold from another
project is not a baseline for this one.

## How readiness works, and why you rarely need to tune it

Lightning boots async, keeps long-poll connections open forever (so `networkidle`
never fires), and renders into **shadow DOM** (so `document.querySelector` cannot
see its components). The tool therefore waits on a signal that needs no knowledge
of Salesforce internals: **the page stopped changing.**

Specifically: text length steady **and** no DOM mutation, across **all frames**, for
2500ms in the described implementation; confirm the selected tool's current
settings. Text can stabilize before all components arrive, an iframe can load
while the main frame is quiet, and persistent network connections can outlive
rendering. A quiet window is a heuristic, not proof that required content loaded.

Practical consequences:

- **Do not pass `settle` after a click.** Interaction steps auto-wait for quiet.
  Adding `settle` *disables* that and reverts you to guessing.
- `--wait <mode>` (`auto`, `record`, `list`, `edit`, `setup`, `none`) is only a
  speed hint. `auto` works on every page family, including Object Manager (which
  lives on a different domain and matches no standard content selector).
- Setup / Object Manager pages are a Lightning+Aura+Visualforce mix and are slower
  and uglier than anything you ship. Prefer testing real front-end pages.
- After deploying an LWC, add `--hard-refresh` to defeat a stale compiled bundle.
- Raise `--settle` only for genuinely animated content, e.g. dashboards.

## Clicking: selector vs coordinates

Both dispatch **real mouse/keyboard events via CDP**, never a JS `.click()`.

- `click: "<selector>"` -- Playwright hit-tests and enforces actionability. If a
  human could not click it (covered by an overlay, hidden, disabled), the step
  **fails** rather than silently passing. That is the QA-correct behaviour and the
  main reason not to use JS clicks.
- `clickAt: [x, y]` -- raw coordinates, zero DOM knowledge. Use this when you have
  just looked at a screenshot and want to click what you see. Coordinates are in
  CSS pixels of the viewport (`--viewport`), not the retina pixels of the PNG:
  with the default `--scale 2`, divide the pixel position in the image by 2.

## Useful flags

| Flag | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--full-page` | Whole scrollable page, not just the viewport |
| `--selector <css>` | Crop to one component (e.g. a single LWC) |
| `--mask <css,css>` | Cover elements, redact PII before sharing |
| `--dismiss` | Close toasts / walkthrough tooltips / splash modals first |
| `--viewport 390x844` | Mobile-width rendering |
| `--headed` | Watch it run, for debugging |
| `--hard-refresh` | Reload bypassing HTTP cache, stale LWC after a deploy |
| `--slow-threshold <ms>` | Flag slow pages as a finding (calibrate per org) |
| `--text` | Write visible page text (grep this to verify values) |

## Sessions

Inspect the selected tool's session configuration before use. Reuse a cached
session only after verifying its org and account match the task. Keep cookies in
private storage outside packages and reports. A username or matching alias alone
does not authorize reuse in another account context.

When supported by the selected tool, `sfqa session --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS
--refresh` renews that session and `--clear` removes it. Authentication changes
remain separate authorized account actions. Do not silently choose a cached org.

## Credential safety (why this is safe to run unattended)

- **No bearer token is ever handled.** Auth redeems a **single-use** frontdoor URL
  from `sf org open --url-only`, consumed in-process by `page.goto()`. It is burned
  by that one navigation. The legacy `frontdoor.jsp?sid=<accessToken>` trick is
  *not* used and no longer works on current orgs anyway.
- The URL is never printed. Every byte the process writes passes through a
  redaction filter that scrubs `otp`/`cshc`/`sid`/token shapes, including from
  uncaught exceptions and Playwright errors that quote the URL.
- Playwright tracing and HAR recording are deliberately disabled; both would
  persist the session cookie to disk.
- **Never** run `sf org open --url-only` or `sf org display --json` yourself and
  paste the output. That puts a live credential in the transcript. Let the tool
  consume them internally.

## Gotchas

- Deploy succeeding is not verification, and neither is a green `ready`. Look at
  the PNG, and grep the `.txt`.
- On failure the tool writes `<out>.FAILED.png`. Check it first when diagnosing.
- Screenshots are retina (`--scale 2`), so a 1600x1000 viewport yields a 3200x2000
  PNG. Use `--scale 1` for smaller files.
- Inspect the actual browser path and supported launch policy before running. The tool configuration does not override the prohibition on direct installed macOS Chrome launches. Record any headless rendering limits.
- Each invocation uses a fresh browser profile, so the HTTP cache is always cold
  between runs. Stale LWC bundles only matter *within* one batch/flow run.

Lightning boots async, keeps long-poll connections open forever (so networkidle never fires), and renders into shadow DOM (so document.querySelector cannot see its components). The tool therefore waits on a signal that needs no knowledge of Salesforce internals: the page stopped changing.

Specifically: text length steady and no DOM mutation, across all frames, for 2500ms in the described implementation; confirm the selected tool's current settings. Text can stabilize before all components arrive, an iframe can load while the main frame is quiet, and persistent network connections can outlive rendering. A quiet window is a heuristic, not proof that required content loaded.

Practical consequences:

  • Do not pass settle after a click. Interaction steps auto-wait for quiet.

Adding settle *disables* that and reverts you to guessing.

  • --wait <mode> (auto, record, list, edit, setup, none) is only a

speed hint. auto works on every page family, including Object Manager (which lives on a different domain and matches no standard content selector).

  • Setup / Object Manager pages are a Lightning+Aura+Visualforce mix and are slower

and uglier than anything you ship. Prefer testing real front-end pages.

  • After deploying an LWC, add --hard-refresh to defeat a stale compiled bundle.
  • Raise --settle only for genuinely animated content, e.g. dashboards.

Clicking: selector vs coordinates

Both dispatch real mouse/keyboard events via CDP, never a JS .click().

  • click: "<selector>" -- Playwright hit-tests and enforces actionability. If a

human could not click it (covered by an overlay, hidden, disabled), the step fails rather than silently passing. That is the QA-correct behaviour and the main reason not to use JS clicks.

  • clickAt: [x, y] -- raw coordinates, zero DOM knowledge. Use this when you have

just looked at a screenshot and want to click what you see. Coordinates are in CSS pixels of the viewport (--viewport), not the retina pixels of the PNG: with the default --scale 2, divide the pixel position in the image by 2.

Useful flags

FlagWhy
--full-pageWhole scrollable page, not just the viewport
--selector <css>Crop to one component (e.g. a single LWC)
--mask <css,css>Cover elements, redact PII before sharing
--dismissClose toasts / walkthrough tooltips / splash modals first
--viewport 390x844Mobile-width rendering
--headedWatch it run, for debugging
--hard-refreshReload bypassing HTTP cache, stale LWC after a deploy
--slow-threshold <ms>Flag slow pages as a finding (calibrate per org)
--textWrite visible page text (grep this to verify values)

Sessions

Inspect the selected tool's session configuration before use. Reuse a cached session only after verifying its org and account match the task. Keep cookies in private storage outside packages and reports. A username or matching alias alone does not authorize reuse in another account context.

When supported by the selected tool, sfqa session --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS --refresh renews that session and --clear removes it. Authentication changes remain separate authorized account actions. Do not silently choose a cached org.

Credential safety (why this is safe to run unattended)

  • No bearer token is ever handled. Auth redeems a single-use frontdoor URL

from sf org open --url-only, consumed in-process by page.goto(). It is burned by that one navigation. The legacy frontdoor.jsp?sid=<accessToken> trick is *not* used and no longer works on current orgs anyway.

  • The URL is never printed. Every byte the process writes passes through a

redaction filter that scrubs otp/cshc/sid/token shapes, including from uncaught exceptions and Playwright errors that quote the URL.

  • Playwright tracing and HAR recording are deliberately disabled; both would

persist the session cookie to disk.

  • Never run sf org open --url-only or sf org display --json yourself and

paste the output. That puts a live credential in the transcript. Let the tool consume them internally.

Gotchas

  • Deploy succeeding is not verification, and neither is a green ready. Look at

the PNG, and grep the .txt.

  • On failure the tool writes <out>.FAILED.png. Check it first when diagnosing.
  • Screenshots are retina (--scale 2), so a 1600x1000 viewport yields a 3200x2000

PNG. Use --scale 1 for smaller files.

  • Inspect the actual browser path and supported launch policy before running. The tool configuration does not override the prohibition on direct installed macOS Chrome launches. Record any headless rendering limits.
  • Each invocation uses a fresh browser profile, so the HTTP cache is always cold

between runs. Stale LWC bundles only matter *within* one batch/flow run.
